articleTitle: Design Considerations for GaN-based Drive-train Inverters in Light Electric-Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Design of high efficiency and high power density drive-train inverters is needed for meeting design targets in 2-wheeler EV segment. Gallium-nitride (GaN)-based inverters offer improvements in both metrics. However, design considerations like voltage levels, operating frequency and thermal performance need to be studied in detail. This paper discusses the indispensable design considerations of device voltage rating, thermal management and operating switching frequency for GaN inverters. Results of a numerical simulation based comparative analysis show that the 150 V DC-link GaN inverter design offers the least losses at a 10 kW power rating, resulting in an estimated power density of 40 kW/L and reduction in cooling system size.

articleTitle: Modular-three-level buck converter for electrolyzer applications: current control with capacitors voltage balancing control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a DC-DC buck converter topology with multi-output capability for stacks of electrolyzers. The converter operation and its behavior are explained through the derivation of differential equations. A control strategy is proposed to regulate the hydrogen production rate effectively. To alleviate the voltage rating requirements of the utilized devices, a series of input capacitors is employed. This configuration reduces the voltage rating burden on individual capacitors by dividing the overall voltage across multiple capacitors. Additionally, a voltage balancing control scheme is introduced to address any potential imbalance in the input capacitor voltages. The proposed converter topology and its controllers are validated through extensive simulations using the circuit-based Simscape tool in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode MRAS Observer for PMSM-fed Electric Vehicle Control using Recurrent Neural Network-Based Parallel Resistance Estimator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a sensorless speed control method for permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) driven electric vehicles (EVs). Typically, PMSMs require rotor position information for vector control, but position sensors can be unreliable, prone to failure in harsh conditions compared to other electrical components, and are expensive. Therefore, speed estimation is preferred over a speed sensor for fault-tolerant operation and cost reduction. The sliding mode observer-based model-reference adaptive control (SMO-MRAS) observer estimates the speed and stator resistance. In contrast, the SMO-MRAS observer performs well in medium and high-speed operations. However, parameter sensitivity makes the SMO-MRAS observer less effective at low speeds. Stator resistance is bound to change as the temperature varies. It is necessary to have an appropriate online identification algorithm to address this issue. A parallel stator resistance using a recurrent neural network (RNN) and rotor speed observer based on SMO-MRAS has been proposed in this article. The MATLAB/Simulink results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the overall control scheme.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Effect of Control Design on Bidirectional Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper applies a two-degree-of-freedom (2DOF) control and a general PI control to a bidirectional dynamic wireless power transfer system. The results of these applications are then compared. The experiments have demonstrated that the 2DOF control improves the transmission energy by 27.0% during grid-to-vehicle (G2V) operation and 27.5% during vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase-Unit Axial-Modular Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine With Integral-Slot Non-Overlapping Concentrated Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a novel phase-unit axial-modular permanent magnet vernier machine (PUAM-PMVM) with integral-slot non-overlapping concentrated windings (ISONCW) is proposed, and the machine phases are split axially with a fixed mechanical angle to produce a steady torque. To start with, the machine theoretical working principle is illustrated and derived theoretically, and the working principle is clarified to validate the proposed topology. Secondly, the slot-pole combinations of this novel PMVM are investigated, which can extend the slot-pole combinations. Then, the performances among the proposed ICONCW, conventional winding topologies are compared and analyzed by finite-element analysis (FEA). Besides, the no-load back-EMF, flux density, power factor, as well as torque are conducted and compared, which can validate the high-torque and superior fault-tolerant capabilities of the proposed PUAM-PMVM. Finally, the conclusions and future prospects are given and developed.

articleTitle: Operational Flexibility of Grid-Connected Power Converters for Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy in modern power systems, inverter-based resources (IBRs) are dominant in power generation. The characteristics of the power system are changing due to the integration. This change demands strongly the controllability and flexibility of renewable power plants (RPPs). A flexible operation framework for RPPs is thus proposed in this paper to address relevant issues. And solutions to the operational flexibility of RPPs are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Non-isolated Onboard EV Charger Controller Design Based on Port-Hamiltonian Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The growth of the electric vehicles (EVs) market and the inadequacy of EV infrastructure, especially EV charging station, have led to an increase in charging EVs at home or the workplace. Onboard EV chargers (OBCs) have been installed on electric vehicles to charge batteries. The trend of increasing power rating and minimized sizing of OBCs, the improvement in stability and performance has been interesting. This paper demonstrates non-isolated EV onboard chargers with controller design based on Port-Hamiltonian control law to approach a robust control system and operate under wide operating range. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed control scheme is validated through experiment in laboratory.

articleTitle: An Iterative Learning Control Method for Non-Repetitive Electric Vehicle Battery Discharging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, an iterative learning control (ILC) problem of electric vehicle (EV) battery state-of-charge (SoC) profile is exploited, because of the identical driving routes daily. Due to the variations on departure and return times as well as traffic conditions, the daily SoC profile is not the same, but could be slightly different from one working day to the other. This paper, therefore, proposes a novel ILC algorithm to deal with such daily-varying characteristic of battery SoC profiles, namely a quadratic ILC (Q-ILC) law with an iteration-varying weighting matrix for the control input update. It is then proved that the proposed ILC law is rapidly converged after just one iteration, under suitable selections of the Q-ILC weighting matrices. Numerical simulations are carried out, whose results validate the superior performance of the proposed ILC algorithm. As such, the proposed ILC scheme has the great potential for rapidly achieving a desired, predicted SoC profile of the EV battery in the next day, and hence, would help save the EV energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Fault-Tolerant Multilevel Inverter (FT-MLI) Topology for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In medium and high-power applications, multilevel inverters (MLIs) are becoming popular due to their low harmonic distortion and reduced voltage stress across switches. Multilevel inverter topologies rely heavily on the reliability of semiconductor devices. In this paper, a new fault-tolerant multilevel inverter topology has been proposed which can work in a different mode of operation with different open-circuit fault (OCF) conditions with the addition of six auxiliary switches to the main circuit which comprises of seven switches and three dc voltage sources. Based on the voltage magnitude of dc voltage sources, proposed FT-MLI topology can be operated in different modes of operation which has been explained in this paper. Further, a fault analysis has been carried out for single and multi-switch OCFs. Finally, simulation results for different fault scenarios have been presented and results have been summarized.

articleTitle: Day-ahead charging load forecasting of electric bus fast charging station based on CEEMDAN-SSALSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: At present, the most urgent problem to be solved in forecasting the charging load of electric bus fast charging station (FCS) is that the precision and accuracy of the forecasting models proposed by existing studies are not high enough. Complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) algorithm based on Gaussian white noise decomposes the historical charging load data into several intrinsic mode functions (IMF) and a residual component (Res) with different frequencies and complexities, and the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is used to obtain the optimal control variables of the long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network. Based on the above two algorithms, CEEMDAN-SSA-LSTM model is constructed to forecast charging load of electric bus FCS. Taking the historical charging load data of Beijing Longjinyuan electric bus FCS as an example, the experiment shows that the prediction accuracy of the this combined model are greatly improved when comparing with the LSTM and CEEMDAN-LSTM model.

articleTitle: A Guideline on PV-Battery Sizing of RE100 Microgrid in Building
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, determination of the sizing of Photovoltaic (PV) installed capacity and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is studied to achieve a 100% renewable energy (RE100) microgrid in building. Firstly, the installed capacity of PV is considered from the accumulation of load-demand energy. Secondly, the net-load energy is examined in three-time frames, minute, day, and week. Thirdly, the sizing of battery is considered by the proposed approach in which the battery capacity is allocated to various reserves, including weeks-ahead, days-ahead, and minutes-ahead. Finally, a three-dimensional graph of PV-battery capacity for RE100 is created as a guideline on optimal sizing selection. The proposed guideline is validated by simulation using MATLAB software with the input from real-world data sets of the building’s load and PV generation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Dual Active Bridge Converter for Hybrid Battery-Supercapacitor Energy Storage System for Electric Bicycles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The paper proposes the simulation model to determine power sharing between supercapacitor and Li-ion battery of hybrid energy storage system (HESS) for electric bicycles. The power delivering from HESS is controlled by dual active bridge converter (DAB). The paper presents the uses of two DAB converters to independently regulate the power of battery and supercapacitor. The simulation results present the requirement of surge power for electric bicycles can be provided by supercapacitor. In addition, high regenerative power is also received by supercapacitor. These can prevent the battery from supplying high inrush current and from getting heat.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 2.4KW CLLC Resonant Dual Active Bridge Converter with Different Phase Shift Modulation Techniques for EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge Converter is prominently used in Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems due to the numerous advantages it offers. The advantages offered by the DAB Converter are galvanic isolation, bidirectional power flow, high voltage gain, high power density and high efficiency. The DAB converter is controlled by employing Phase Shift Modulation (PSM) techniques. The efficiency of the DAB converter is increased by using resonant tank circuit in series with the isolation transformer in conjunction with various advanced modulation schemes. In this work, design and implementation of CLLC Resonant Dual Active Bridge (DAB) Converter for Electric Vehicle (EV) battery charging application is presented. The DAB converter connected to the common DC bus of Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) is controlled by employing various Phase Shift Modulation (PSM) schemes such as Single Phase Shift (SPS), Dual Phase Shift (DPS) and Triple Phase Shift (TPS) modulation. The performance of the CLLC DAB Converter is analyzed for the different cases. The EV battery pack of 240V is connected to the output of DAB converter. The battery pack is charged at a constant current of 10A. The designed system is validated through simulations performed in MATLAB/Simulink followed by hardware implementation using OP4610.

Author Keywords: CLLC Resonant Dual Active Bridge Converter

articleTitle: One-Loop Model-Free Torque Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The primary objective of this research paper is to implement a model-free control strategy for a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) that is powered by a Voltage Source Inverter (VSI). The proposed control approach has several benefits, including improved transient response and increased bandwidth. In addition to outlining the one-loop control architecture, this paper also explores ways to limit the saturation of state variables to improve system robustness against unexpected disturbances. Through simulation results, the study evaluates the performance of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Torque Controller for an IPMSM using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for torque control in electric drive systems using reinforcement learning (RL). The traditional field-oriented control (FOC) in an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM) is replaced with an RL-based controller developed using the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm in Simulink. The RL agent is trained to determine optimal voltage values for the IPMSM in the dq-plane, considering observations and reward functions tailored to the torque control problem. The reward function incorporates constraints to prevent training on negative torque and speed values and exceeding maximum motor values. Comparative simulation results and analysis demonstrate the performance of the RL-based torque controller, emphasizing its advantages over FOC in terms of adaptability and torque response without requiring a precise mathematical model of the system. This research contributes to the advancement of electric drive control, showcasing the potential of RL algorithms to enhance torque behavior and adaptability in electrical drives.

Author Keywords: Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)

articleTitle: Model Predictive-Position Sensorless Control of PMSM with Non-Sinusoidal Back-EMF
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has proven to be an efficient control technique for torque ripple minimization in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). The torque ripple in practical PMSM is primarily caused by the non-sinusoidal back-EMF owing to the exact shape and structure of the rotor magnets and the equivalent non-sinusoidal flux distribution within the air gap. The predictive control techniques use the rotor flux lookup table (LUT) to estimate the motor output torque under non-sinusoidal back-EMF. This work proposes a rotor position estimation technique by using the rotor flux LUT and by reverse calculating the α and β components of the rotor flux components from the measured motor phase currents and inverter control signals. The proposed technique estimates the rotor angle irrespective of the initial position without requiring additional sensors. The sensorless control is modeled and tested in the simulation environment for a PMSM of 7 kW rated power, and the design is validated.

articleTitle: A Reduction of Entire Common-Mode Voltage by Self-Cancelling Technique for Two-Stage Transformerless PV Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Reduction of common-mode voltages in the two-stage PV inverter is challenging once both common-mode voltages generated from boost converter and three-phase inverter are arisen concurrently. This paper proposes an entire common-mode voltage reduction technique for two-stage PV inverters by using the degree of freedom from the zero-sequence voltage of three-phase inverter. The selection of such zero-sequence voltage makes the cooperation between pulse-width modulations of boost converter and inverter, and consequently conducts a self-cancellation of common-mode voltages. The proposed technique is established without added active and passive components, and the experimental results from the real-world commercial product examine its performance. The entire common-mode voltage can be reduced satisfactorily in the wide frequency range, which results in the accomplished reduction of leakage current.

articleTitle: Control of Three-Level PWM Inverter-Fed Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents the control of three-level PWM committed to a three-level twelve-switch inverter-fed induction motor drive. The proposed control is totally capable of extracting the maximum DC utilization with the classical continuous and discontinuous PWM. Moreover, in the light of the multi-level inherency, the low switching frequency is attractive to this application to avoid the high power losses, while it can maintain the stability of the operation. Regardless of the single or double carrier waves, optimized switching states associated with the proposed logical operation part, which is responsible for obtaining the multi-level characteristic of the inverter, are also proposed. Importantly, through the MATLAB/Simulink program, the steady-state and dynamic response of the high-performance drive with the classically indirect vector control are definitely investigated to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Power Compensation Control of Electrolytic Capacitor-Less Dual-Inverter to Extend Motor Operating Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a power compensation control for open-end winding interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (OEW-IPMSMs) driven by electrolytic capacitor-less dual inverters with single-phase power supplies. The dual inverter operates with both high-power factor of a single-phase source and a constant torque of the motor. In addition, the additional inverter compensates for a reactive power of the motor, which allows the original inverter to operate at unity power factor condition, thus extending the motor operating region. Simulations and experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed power compensation control and extending the motor operating region.

articleTitle: Influence of Annealing on the Iron Loss of Amorphous Alloy High-speed Permanent Magnet Motors Based on the Preisach Hysteresis Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Amorphous alloys are of great concern in high-speed applications due to high magnetic permeability and low iron losses, but the production process has a significant impact on the performance of amorphous alloy stator cores. In this paper, by using the ring specimen experiment, the influence of annealing temperature on the performance of amorphous alloy stator core is analyzed, including hysteresis loops, magnetization curves, and iron loss curves. The Preisach hysteresis model and the loss separation model are used separately to calculate the iron losses of amorphous alloy high-speed permanent magnet motors under different annealing temperatures. The results show that the high-speed permanent magnet motor has the minimum iron loss when the amorphous alloy stator core is incomplete annealed.

articleTitle: Design of a GaN-Based Power Converter for Small-Sized Integrated Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The integrated motor drive concept, which combines the motor and power converter into a single entity, is a significant emerging trend in the field of motor systems. Integrated motor drives offer several benefits, including complexity reduction and cost reduction. However, integrating power converters into motors poses challenges, especially for small-sized servo motors. This paper presents a novel design of a GaN-based power converter that addresses this issue. The proposed power converter is compact in size and features a circular shape, facilitating seamless integration with the motor. The prototype power converter has been fabricated and tested. The experimental results for the prototype power converter operation are presented, which verify its feasibility to drive low-power motors and demonstrate its promising performance for integrated motor drives.

articleTitle: An Implementation of Fault-Current Boosting Technique for Inverter-Based Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The growth of renewable energy sources and microgrid systems is becoming challenges in various aspects of the electrical power system. The focus of this paper is to address the decrease in fault current levels since inverters cannot inject a high fault current similar to synchronous generators in conventional electrical system. This issue becomes crucial when the microgrid operates in islanding mode. In this paper, a fault current boosting technique for grid-connected inverters is proposed, by using the resonance frequency of the inverter’s LCL filter to enlarge the output current up to 2 times of the inverter rated current. The inverter will switch from normal operation to low voltage operation when a fault occurs in the system and revert to normal operation when the fault is cleared. The proposed algorithm is stimulated using Matlab/Simulink and confirmed by laboratory testing with a 3kVA three-phase inverter. The results demonstrate that the inverter can inject high-frequency current and enlarge the current at the point of common coupling (PCC) to 2.4 times the inverter’s output current, while output current of inverter does not exceed its rating. The inverter remains connected throughout the low voltage period and switches back to normal operation when the voltage at PCC returns to the nominal voltage.

articleTitle: A Various-Time-Frame Frequency Control of Grid-forming Inverter for RE100 Microgrid in Building
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A microgrid in building is studied, and it aims to achieve 100% renewable energy (RE100) utilization by integrating Photovoltaic (PV) and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) into the building. The grid-forming inverter plays a crucial role in maintaining frequency stability, especially in islanded mode. This paper proposes a frequency-control structure of grid-forming inverter for the BESS that emulates the characteristics of a synchronous generator, including virtual inertia and power-frequency droop in primary control. Additionally, secondary control with an Area Control Error (ACE) scheme is included to regulate the tie-line power flow and to restore the frequency to its nominal value. The performance of grid-forming inverter is evaluated by the simulation using DIgSILENT Powerfactory program. The real-world data sets of actual load in building and PV electricity generation are employed; the grid forming inverter can achieve the RE100 function in grid-connected mode and attain the frequency stability in the islanded mode.

articleTitle: A Simple Clamping Method to Suppress Switching Oscillation for SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) power metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) provides a system-level performance improvement in power electronics applications due to their excellent performance compared to silicon-based devices. However, the advantages of the low on-resistance and fast switching speed of the device can also cause undesired switching behavior in practice, such as severe switching oscillations, which can lead to device breakdown and damage. This paper proposes a clamping method to suppress switching oscillations, mainly using some passive devices, which makes the design simple. In addition, the proposed method makes it possible to greatly reduce the switching oscillations without affecting the switching speed of the device due to the role of the clamping capacitor, which will not increase the switching losses. Finally, an experimental platform is built to verify the theoretical analysis, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: 6-Slot/2-Pole Permanent Magnet Motors with Non-overlapping Two Coil-Pitch Windings for Ultra-High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper, a 6-slot/2-pole ultra-high-speed permanent magnet (UHSPM) motor with non-overlapping 2 coil-pitch windings is designed for industrial and domestic applications. The proposed UHSPM motor is optimized for maximum torque density considering stator thermal limitation. Its electromagnetic performance and mechanical strength are evaluated by the finite element method, together with the investigation on the influence of winding connection types and rotor eccentricities. As will be shown, the non-overlapping 2 coil-pitch windings offer advantages of short end-winding axial length, high torque density, and high rotor mechanical strength. The series winding connection is superior to the parallel connection since the unbalanced inductances and resistances of two parallel-connected coils in one phase result in circulating currents and unbalanced magnetic force. Several predicted results are validated by experiments based on a prototype motor.

articleTitle: Flux Modulated Motor Using Magnetic-Geared Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper focuses on a flux modulated motor that consists of 3 parts: inner rotor, middle rotor, and stator. The inner rotor can be rotated when the middle rotor is fixed, and the middle rotor can be rotated when the inner rotor is fixed. In this way, this motor has 2 operation modes. The torque-speed characteristics of 2 operation modes is compared, and the difference is discussed.

articleTitle: Contribution of a tunnel to train-running energy consumption for Nakhon Sawan – Mae Sot Railway Line Project
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This article presents a study of a single train movement with tunnel effect on train-running energy consumption. The Nakhon Sawan-Mae Sot double track railway project has been selected as a test section. Simulation was done on a single train traveling whole trip from Nakhon Sawan through Khamphaeng Phet, Tak and Mae Sot with 27 passenger stations in 247.085 km range including 4 tunnels, 2 twin tunnels and 2 single tunnels with overall length 29.714 km. Simulation work was divided into 2 scenarios namely city train traveling with higher number of stops and express train with a few stops. It also noted that this study excluded gradient in this study.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of an EV lithium iron phosphate battery pack for improved cooling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery packs comprise a significant share of an electric vehicle’s cost, especially for low-cost variants such as those used for public transportation (e.g. jeepneys in the Philippines). These can easily occupy 40% of the vehicle’s cost. In this regard, it is very important to ensure the longevity of the battery cells. Lithium-ion cells which are poorly-managed thermally risk having to be replaced sooner than their intended usable life. Thus, proper attention must be given to the design of the battery packs to allow effective and efficient cooling. This study performed a cooling simulation on prismatic lithium iron phosphate cells using ANSYS Workbench. The simulation looked into (1) the effect of the layout of the cells; (2) the thickness of cooling fins; and (3) the temperature and flow rate of the cooling fluid to the thermal profile of the battery pack. The simulations successfully showed that the recommended operating temperature can be obtained even with a compact layout and using thin cooling fins. Practical considerations such as space constraints on the vehicle and weight of the battery pack outweigh the technical benefits of improved heat transfer efficiency using a more spaced-out battery layout and thicker cooling fins.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis for Electric Vehicle Hosting Capacity in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a short survey of existing studies on sensitivity analysis techniques for evaluating hosting capabilities in distribution networks. With the increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), it is crucial to assess the impact of their integration on the power grid. Sensitivity analysis plays a significant role in understanding the relationship between key parameters and the EV hosting capacity, aiding network planning, management, and policy formulation. This paper explores various methodologies, challenges, and opportunities for further research in sensitivity analysis for EV hosting capacity. Furthermore, a case study on sensitivity analysis of EV hosting capacity in a real-distribution feeder with 966 customers in Australia is demonstrated in this paper. It demonstrates voltage unbalance issues dominate EV hosting capacity due to uneven distribution of residential solar systems.

articleTitle: Exploring Power Electronics Converters for Water Electrolysis in Microgrid Applications: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Hydrogen has changed the future energy structure due to its application in different energy sectors. This energy carrier and its derivatives will play a key role in the decarbonization of different sectors in the near future. Water electrolysis using renewable energies is a key way to produce this energy carrier respecting decarbonization goals. It is noteworthy that nowadays this method is mostly using grid electricity. Meanwhile, the expansion of microgrids using renewable energy sources and the need for these microgrids to store energy makes hydrogen production attractive in this sector. On the other hand, the produced hydrogen can be used not only for the purpose of generating electricity in the microgrid but also for generating heat in the local heating network and as a fuel in the transportation sector. Power electronics converters must be used to match the DC and/or AC voltages in these microgrids with the required voltage of electrolyzers. It is challenging to choose the appropriate converters to optimize the system's efficiency and economy and maximize the electrolyzer's lifetime. This paper aims to review the converters used for the electrolyzer systems in the microgrid structure. It is tried to compare these converters in terms of specific energy, efficiency, and economy.

articleTitle: The Development of Inverter for Electric Propulsion System UAM using Wide-Bandgap Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces the development of a 150kW inverter for electric propulsion such as urban air mobility (UAM). Considering the power density, the silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs were used. A gate driver was designed for safe driving of the SiC modules and on/off characteristic of SiC was optimized through a double pulse test under various load current conditions. In order to increase the reliability of the developed inverter, an overcurrent protection such as DESAT was designed, and the function of the protection circuit was confirmed through the experimental results. The maximum efficiency satisfied 97% and was verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Comparison of Coaxial Magnetic Gears Using Rare Earth and Nonrare Earth Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Mechanical gears are widely used because they allow traction motors with high efficiency at high speed and low torque to be driven with high performance at low speed and high torque. The friction of mechanical gears, however, causes noise and vibration and requires maintenance due to wear. Coaxial magnetic gears (CMGs) can overcome the problems of mechanical gears by transmitting torque without physical contact, but their heavy use of rare earth permanent magnets (PMs) has been an obstacle in the face of unstable supply and price of rare earth PMs. To reduce the dependence on rare earth PMs and increase the cost efficiency, four combinations of CMGs utilizing Neodymium (Nd) and ferrite are proposed. The comparative models were designed to satisfy a gear ratio of 7 with 4 inner PM poles and 28 outer PM poles. From the Lorentz force equation and flux density equation of CMG, it was confirmed that the product of magnetic flux densities of the inner PM and the outer PM is proportional to torque. Further, through the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), it was verified that the harmonics of magnetic flux density product is divided into a component contributing to torque and a loss component converted to vibration. These relationships were validated by the performances of CMGs and the frozen permeability method (FPM) based on 2-dimensional (2D) finite element analysis (FEA). Considering the rare earth dependence, torque ripple, efficiency, and cost analysis of the optimal design results, the ferrite-Nd CMG showed a high potential performance among the proposed optimal models. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of ferrite-Nd CMG through experiments and FEA were compared.

articleTitle: Operating characteristics of adjustable-field permanent magnet motors with 3D magnetic paths and asymmetric magnet arrangement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper describes a three-dimensional structure and a high-power density rotor structure using asymmetric permanent magnet (PM) arrangement of an adjustable-field PM motor aiming to achieve both high-torque and high-efficiency operations in a high-speed and low-torque range. It is demonstrated by 3D-FEA that it is possible to achieve the adjustable-field operation without sacrificing the high-torque density. In addition, the adjustable-field effect was verified through an experimental no-load test by measuring some induced voltages of a prototype motor based on the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modelling and Sizing Framework for Hybrid-Electric Aircraft Architecture Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This project aims to develop an electrical system for a hybrid-electric, regional aircraft as part of the drive towards more sustainable transportation. It wants to reduce the aviation industry’s contribution to carbon emissions, looking at more green sources of power. This paper presents the design method for mathematical models to determine the electrical power system sizing for a parallel hybrid-electric aircraft architecture. The work includes an investigation of the power losses, volume, and weight of the gearbox, electrical machine, power electronic converters, circuit breakers, batteries, and fuel cells. The work shows potential weight savings by increasing machine speed and improving battery specific energy density. This EPS design has been conducted to form part of a larger study aiming to produce a hybrid-electric aircraft design.

articleTitle: Extended Characteristics of Grid-Forming Control: Seen from the Perspective of AC Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The rapid growth of renewable energy sources (RESs) leads to an increasingly higher penetration of power converters in the grid. However, unlike conventional synchronous generators (SGs), power converters are difficult to provide voltage or frequency support. Considering this, the grid-forming (GFM) control has been explored to form a stable voltage reference with a fixed frequency. Although certain regulations and requirements of the GFM control have been released, a unified definition is still missing. In this paper, the characteristics of the GFM are extended seen from the perspective of AC power supply in order to assist the unification of GFM technologies. Case studies have been provided to demonstrate the extended characteristics.

articleTitle: Motor Permanent Magnet Temperature estimation based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is widely used in the traction applications of electric vehicles. One of the ways to increase the output efficiency of the PMSM motor is to accurately estimate parameters. The effectiveness of the Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) based permanent magnet temperature(PMT) estimation method has been verified through some experiment with a traction motor. In this paper, the temperature of the rotor, which affects the fluctuation temperature of the permanent magnet, is estimated by deep neural network model. The temperature of the permanent magnet is caused by losses, and copper loss, iron loss, and other control losses have an effect. However, it is complicated and inaccurate to express the effect of the loss as a formula, and it is difficult to solve the complex formula again when the motor and inverter are changed. Therefore, this paper estimates the rotor temperature based on data.

articleTitle: An Ultrafast State-of-Health Monitoring Scheme for Li-ion Batteries Based on A Simple Electrical Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Fast and accurate detections of state-of-health (SoH) are urgently required by various industrial sectors to facilitate reuse and recycling of Li-ion batteries. However, existing SoH identification methods rarely reconcile both monitoring speed and accuracy, which may result in plenty of electronic wastes. To address this issue, an ultrafast and accurate SoH monitoring scheme based on a least square method with forgetting factors is proposed in this paper. The proposed method is established based on a simple electrical model that can be implemented using cost-effective micro-controller units (MCUs). Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method to detect SoH of one new battery and three old batteries fast and accurately.

Author Keywords: least square method with forgetting factors

articleTitle: A Review on One-Axis Actively Positioned Bearingless Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Bearingless motors with one-axis active positioning are a new class of electric motors that combine motor torque with non-contact magnetic suspension forces, making them suitable for various industrial applications. In this paper, the current status of various aspects related to these motors is presented, highlighting the challenges faced in their development, including improvements in torque density with motor volumes, torque density with the centering index, power, and rotational speed. Furthermore, efficiency and power are compared to those two-, four-, and five-axis actively positioned motors. It was determined that the difficulties encountered included improving the torque density, attaining high efficiency, and increasing rotational speeds.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage DC Motor Driver Based on Class-E Resonant Wireless Power Transfer Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Traditional wired DC motors often face challenges associated with cable, copper losses, and magnetic losses, which can have a notable impact on the efficiency and lifespan of the motors. These losses, arising from the nature of the wired connection, can hamper the overall performance and longevity of DC motors. This paper introduces an innovative solution to the challenges posed by traditional wired DC motors, presenting a single-stage class-E resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) technique that controls the DC motor. The proposed WPT system incorporates an interleaved class-E resonant circuit with zero-voltage switching (ZVS) characteristic at the transmitter (Tx) to amplify the output power and improving reliability, enabling efficient handling of the DC motor's changing load conditions under different speeds. Meanwhile, at the receiver (Rx), a full-bridge phase-shift (FBPS) technique is employed to modulate the phase and control the armature voltage supplied to the DC motor, thereby controlling its speed. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed technique in this paper achieves a maximum efficiency of 96.9% at a phase shift of π.

articleTitle: Power Flow Analysis of Advanced Power Generation Centre for More Electric Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The more-electric aircraft (MEA) has been seen as the most major trend in the aerospace industry. With the increase in electrified loads, there is the need to generate more electrical power on-board aircraft. Considering regional jet sized aircraft, one novel approach is to extract electric power from high-pressure shaft as well as the low-pressure shaft within a multi-spool aircraft engine. This allows for more electrical power extraction within the engine shaft mechanical limits. Furthermore, it opens opportunities to enable power transfer between two different shafts within the engine in order to increase the operational margin and improve efficiency. This system called the Advanced Power Generation Centre (APGC), is introduced in this paper and the associated electrical subsystem with the high-pressure shaft has been analysed in detail. The capabilities and limitations of this topology have been discussed in this paper and validated in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Fibre Bragg Grating Sensor Based Winding Strain Monitoring and Insulation Lifetime Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Fibre Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors have attracted interest for electric machine condition monitoring due to their small size, EMI immunity, multiplexing of individual gratings and robustness in harsh environments. FBG sensors can be placed at key locations within the machine windings which are close to the temperature and stress hot spots. This paper investigates the feasibility of using FBG sensors to monitor the strain of the winding insulation material. The possibility of predicting winding insulation fatigue by generated S-N curve with FBG sensor measured winding strain is explored.

articleTitle: Modified Single Switch Bridgeless PFC Converter based Sensorless PMSM Drive for Exhaust Fan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents sensorless control of the exhaust fan’s permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) using a power factor correction (PFC) converter. The fan initially has an inefficient single-phase induction motor, which is replaced with an energy-efficient PMSM to reduce energy consumption. To address power quality issues, a modified single switch bridgeless PFC SEPIC (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>BL SEPIC) converter is employed. This converter design enhances efficiency by minimizing component count, and conduction losses and eliminating the circulating current. The control strategy prioritizes robustness and simplicity over high-speed performance, using a sensorless approach based on flux estimation to determine the PMSM’s rotor position. The S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>BL SEPIC PFC operates in discontinuous mode, further streamlining the control structure. The upgraded fan operates effectively across a wide input voltage range.

articleTitle: Estimation of Energy Yield of a Solar Roof on EVs with Differential Power Processing Converter using a 3D Model and Validation of the Analytical Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A photovoltaic (PV) panel comprises multiple series-connected substrings of cells, which are then connected in series. In curved PV panels mounted on the roofs of electric vehicles (EVs), variations in electrical characteristics among cells and substrings cause a significant reduction in power generation. As a solution, a Differential Power Processing Converters (DPPCs) has been proposed to improve power generation by quasi-uniformize the electrical characteristics. However, to achieve uniform electrical characteristics across all cells, a combination of cell-level and substring-level DPPCs is required, increasing the system's cost. Therefore, it is desirable to determine the level of DPPC installation by considering the increase in power generation, and an analytical model is needed to predict the power generation of curved PV panels accurately. This paper reproduces the 56-cell PV panel installed in the Prius PHV by 3D model and creates an analytical power generation model. The validity of the analytical model was verified through field tests, and the annual power generation when the DPPC was installed was quantitatively evaluated.

articleTitle: Current Sensor Fault Tolerant strategy for a Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces a fault-tolerant control method for current sensors in a Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine (WRSM). These types of machines are commonly used in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV) setups. The methodology involves estimating stator currents and integrating a comparison algorithm to detect potential faults in the current sensors. Upon identifying a fault in one of the current sensors, the control system smoothly transitions to a sensorless current control mode. The proposed control method utilizes a flux-based model of the WRSM to estimate stator currents and manage the machine during the post-fault period. This transition to sensorless control mode is rapid and has no adverse effects on rotor speed. The performance of the proposed current sensor fault detection and the subsequent sensorless control are validated through simulations and experimental tests conducted on a test bench.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of Power Module with BCI-ROMs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the thermal characterization of SiC MOSFETs within automotive power modules. We employ the thermal transient measurement method, simulation techniques, thermal model calibration procedures, and a boundary condition independent reduces-order model (BCI-ROM) to comprehensively analyze and understand the thermal behavior of theses module. Thermal model calibration using the thermal transient measurement is performed to enhance the accuracy of thermal simulation and improve component reliability. Furthermore, a BCI-ROM is demonstrated for automotive mission power profiles, derived from a fully detailed calibrated model. ROM aims to decrease computational complexity, enabling faster solving while maintaining predictive accuracy in both space and time.

articleTitle: Resynchronization of Grid-Forming Inverter -Stability Analysis and Design Guidelines-
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Transition between islanded and grid-connected operations of grid-forming inverters requires a stable and well-designed voltage synchronization. In this paper, the voltage synchronization scheme of grid-forming inverter is addressed with the stability analysis and design guidelines. The stability conditions of vector Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) are given, and the design guidelines of controllers are provided to achieve the tracking performance. Implementation of 1.6 kVA grid-forming inverter is conducted to validate the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Study of Direct Torque Control during Turns for Electric All-Terrain Vehicles with Two-Wheel Independent Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Wheel Independent drive structures presented improvement of maneuverability and stability of vehicles. In this paper, the study of direct torque control (DTC) regulating two rear hub-motors during turns of electric all-terrain vehicles (ATV) has been proposed. Mathematic models present torque and power requirements of two rear wheels driving in curves. In comparison to axle drives with and without differential gear, the two-wheel independent drive presented a narrower turning radius by means of DTC. The simulation results present the lower peak current and instantaneous power at the battery. In addition, the braking torque of the inner wheel in curves can be achieved by the hub motor.

articleTitle: Mass-Specific Thermal Optimization of a Heat Sink for rotating 80kW SiC Dual Inverter Exposed to Extreme Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The scope of this study encompasses the design of a heat sink for rotating power electronics operating under conditions of significantly elevated temperature within a rotating actuator system which integrates two 40kW SiC inverters for fault-tolerant operation. The primary objective is to identify optimal parameters for designing the rotary heat sink, ensuring efficient heat dissipation while adhering to weight limits and considering space envelope and coolant air constraints. The thermal efficiency of the designed heat sinks is accessed in terms of mass-specific heat transfer coefficient through the computational fluid dynamic analysis. The findings demonstrate that the augmented fin height and thinner fin dimensions lead to enhanced performance. Notably, a larger gap between fins augments the thermal performance of the heat sink under rotation. Conversely, an opposing trend manifests when the heat sink is stationary.

articleTitle: Operation of a Series Resonant Converter as a Dual-Gain DC-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Wide voltage range DC-DC converters use different topological modifications or complex modulation schemes to cover the full range of voltage. However, certain applications do not require the coverage of the full voltage range but distinct voltage levels. Applications with two converter systems of AC-DC and DC-DC converters utilize the capabilities of both the converters to achieve the required output voltages. SRC converter have been known to be used for fixed voltage ratio operation. Using mode switching, SRC converters can facilitate dual voltage gain operation. This simple technique ensures high efficiency without compromising on simplicity. Use of loss cycling between half-bridges further improves the converter reliability.

articleTitle: Switch Fault Detection in a Family of Non-isolated Single-Inductor Three-Port Converters for Low Power Electrification Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a novel family of non-isolated single inductor three-port converters with built-in switch fault detection capability. Compared to conventional converters, these converters require minimal additional components while offering four control degrees of freedom. Through analysis and simulations, their effectiveness in meeting energy management requirements is demonstrated. The fault detection method relies on monitoring inductor current shape and switching command values, enabling timely fault identification. This integration of advanced energy management and fault detection makes these converters promising for power electronic applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Phase-Shift Algorithm for Single-Shunt Current Sensing with Two-Arm Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Single-Shunt Resistor is typically used to detect inverter currents due to the cost of electronics components or circuits. However, for an inverter implemented with Space Vector PWM, the single-shunt method cannot sense a current in some regions of the current waveforms that occur when one active switching state in a switching period has inadequate state time to use for measuring an inverter current. In case of three-arm modulation, Phase-Shift algorithm is represented to reduce this immeasurable problem by shifting the modulated signals of an inverter such that the active state has enough sensing time, and the three-phase current can be all detected. This paper is a study of phase-shift algorithm for single-shunt current sensing while using two-arm modulation and its condition, as well as the limitations occurred from this method.

articleTitle: A Leakage-Current Reduction Technique for Two-Stage Transformerless PV Inverters with Consideration of Resonant Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a leakage-current reduction technique for commercial transformerless grid-connected 2-stage PV inverters. The switching-frequency component of common-mode voltage is examined by Fourier series, and it is reduced by the selection of the optimal zero-sequence voltages among the 2-arm modulation schemes. In addition, the resonant phenomenon in PV system is investigated. By insertion of a bypass capacitor in the common-mode model, the obstacle from this phenomenon can be alleviated by relocating the resonant frequency of the PV system to be lower than that of the switching frequency. Both simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly reduce the leakage current to comply with VDE-0126-1-1 standard, and also successfully avoid the drawback from resonant phenomenon.

articleTitle: Another Novel Concept Selection of Hexagonal Switching State Vector for DPC of a Three-Phase PWM Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Three-phase AC/DC PWM rectifier is an important front-end part which is prepares high-level DC voltage as well as good quality input current (Power Factor Correction: PFC) waveforms for DC fast charging of electric vehicles (EVs). The concept of Direct Power Control (DPC) is an appropriate technique for this rectifier due to its robustness and fast dynamic. However, the DPC needs an empirical hexagonal switching pattern to achieve good quality of input current waveforms. In this paper, based on the DPC, the concept of different angles between grid voltage vector and rectifier voltage vector is proposed for undoubtedly defining the table of hexagonal switching state vector. Consequently, compared to the conventional one, the quality of input current waveforms of the proposed concept is significantly improved. Experimental results of the proposed concept are realized by a 3kW prototype rectifier.

articleTitle: Increasing Hosting Capacity for Electric Vehicles in Unbalanced Distribution Systems by Three-Phase Step Voltage Regulators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of voltage control of unbalanced distribution systems incorporating a three-phase step voltage regulator (3ϕSVR) on electric vehicle (EV) hosting capacity. The EV charging loads are modeled using arrival time data. In the voltage control, 3ϕSVR is coordinated with the active and reactive power output control of smart inverters and a load-ratio control transformer. The IEEE 13 node test feeder is used for power flow simulation to investigate unbalanced EV integration into distribution systems, and hosting capacity is analyzed in a case study.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of On-Grid Park & Ride EV Parking Station Considering Dynamic Pricing in Japan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In recent years, achieving a decarbonized society has necessitated reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Many countries set goals to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions during each of these periods. To achieve this goal, the introduction of carbon dioxide-free Electric Vehicles will be effective. In this paper, we propose an on-grid Park & Ride parking station to charge EVs with PV and WG. We also showed that the dynamic pricing case with varying electricity prices is better than the constant electricity price case. Variable prices encourage the purchase of electricity during the hours when electricity price is low. Such price cases contribute the reduction of operating costs.

articleTitle: Investigation of ToU and V2G to Accommodate High EV Penetrations in Power Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric utilities and Distribution System Operators (DSO) are becoming more apprehensive about the potentially negative effects of uncontrolled Electric Vehicle (EV) charging on their distribution grids. However, implementing appropriate measures such as Time-of-Use (ToU) tariff and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) capability can help mitigate these negative effects and accommodate more EV integration into the power distribution grid. This paper investigates the effectiveness of utilizing ToU and V2G as controlled mechanisms from a DSO standpoint to facilitate high EV penetrations. The study utilized the open-source Dynamic Phasor Simulator (DPSim) as a real-time power flow simulator and incorporated the Power Management algorithm while employing the lightweight Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol as the hardware-in-the-loop communication interface. The study concludes that the implementation of controlled mechanisms can reduce the impacts of voltage quality without necessitating infrastructure upgrades or causing inconvenience to EV users.

articleTitle: State of Health Battery Estimation by Using the OCPP of Charging Station Combined with Loss of EV Charging System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The research paper focuses on estimating the health of electric vehicle batteries using electrical variables measured by the charger during the charging process. These variables are sent to a central processing system via OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol), as the charger itself has limitations in directly measuring battery health. To overcome this limitation, this research utilizes electrical variables measured by the DC charger during the charging process to estimate battery health. The Coulomb counting method is employed in combination with an investigation into losses within the vehicle's charging system to enhance the accuracy of State of Health (SoH) estimation. The obtained battery health values will assist electric vehicle users in better trip planning and maintenance scheduling.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor for Direct Drive Multi-car Elevator Variable Rail System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of multi-car operation of long-stroke ropeless elevator, this paper uses 22-pole 24-slot permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM ) as the driving source to determine the multi-car rail change scheme of elevator and the motor parameters that meet the operation requirements. The boot-type end teeth are added on both sides of the motor to improve the end effect of the motor and improve the operating stability to meet the requirements of the smooth operation of the motor. In order to maximize the effect of suppressing the end effect of the boot-shaped end teeth, the multi-objective optimization method of response surface method (RSM) combined with particle swarm optimization (PSM) is used to optimize the boot-shaped end teeth with thrust, thrust fluctuation and magnetic resistance as the optimization objectives. The electromagnetic characteristics of the motor are analyzed by finite element comparison, and the optimization results are verified by prototype experiments. The results show that the electromagnetic performance index of the optimized PMLSM is improved, and it can be better applied to the direct drive rail changing occasions.

articleTitle: On the use of parametric stator models for electrical machine vibration computation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Parametric stator structural models are used in the electrical machine optimization process and in system-level simulations for noise and vibration prediction. In this paper different models that differ in computational resources and prediction accuracy are explored. First, the analytical method used for stator eigen-frequencies computation is statistically compared with the finite-element method. Afterwards, the vibration displacement computed via the semi-analytical method, that uses an analytical formulation for the forced response, including modulation effects and tangential force factors, and eigen-frequencies coming from finite element analysis, is statistically compared with the results produced by the vibration-synthesis method, representing a pure finite-element method. Here, the air-gap forces excitation used in the forced response problem are computed using a finite-element electromagnetic parametric model. The trade-offs between computation time and model accuracy are discussed.

articleTitle: Adaptable EV DC charger station design using matrix switch network with series connection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A major challenge for fast DC charging of electric vehicles (EVs) is the wide range of battery voltages available for different types of vehicle. By using a matrix switch network in EV charging stations to connect EV charger modules (EVCM) in series and/or parallel, widely different voltages and power can be delivered at the charging station. Functional integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) can be realized without any additional power converter. Using a two-step charging technique enables EVCMs with a narrow output voltage range to deliver different charging voltages with faster charging. By connecting the charging stations in a mesh, ring, or star topology, flexible deployment and full utilization of installed charging power can be achieved. A future-proof charging park can be thus constructed using EVCM with 500V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> output.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer System for Autonomous Driving Robot Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a prototype of a 48V, 200W with 85 kHz wireless power transfer. The load-independent charging topology consists of an LCC/C resonant tank that provides an autonomous driving robot that is used in many industrial applications. The validation is carried out using MATLAB/Simulink and hardware implementation. The rear side battery can apparently be charged with a 15cm distance between two coils and the output voltage can be controlled at a specific level with approximately 70% efficiency.

articleTitle: Real-Time Initialization of Thermal Models of an Oil- Cooled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Model-based thermal monitoring and control are of great importance for electrical machines. This work outlines the modeling approach for lumped parameter thermal networks for an oil-cooled permanent magnet machine. For real-time applications, the initialization of the thermal models is a challenge, especially for models with highly resolved temperature distributions. To overcome that, a neural network is trained to represent the lumped parameter thermal model, which is able to predict the initial thermal state immediately and to reduce the convergence time enormously. The experimental validation conducted on the test bench confirms the accuracy and the initialization capability of the neural network in real-time.

articleTitle: Torque Feedback MTPA Control Using Flux Approximation Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The optimal operation point of Interior Permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs) deviates from the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) operating point by parameter change. To cope with this problem, the flux approximation surface against current vector is applied to the torque feedback control. In this paper, a calculation method in the controller is proposed by a linearization method.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Direct AC-AC Wireless Power Transfer System Using Conduction Mode-Exchanged Pulse Density Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a new prototype of a single-phase, direct ac-ac converter for inductive wireless power transfer (WPT) applications. The proposed WPT features a power control methodology based on pulse density modulation (PDM) suitable for a wide range of soft switching and fixed frequency operation, which is beneficial for switching loss minimization and circuit parameter design. The essential performances of the proposed system are investigated by an experiment of a 25-kHz small-scale prototype, whereby the direct ac-ac power conversion and PDM-based power control characteristics with wide-range soft switching are revealed.

articleTitle: Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis of NPC Three-Level Inverter Based on Stator Voltage Errors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents an open circuit fault diagnosis method of NPC three-level inverter based on stator voltage error. The three-phase stator voltage error is taken as the characteristic quantity, and the fault phase is quickly located by comparing the magnitude, positive and negative relationship between the stator voltage errors of different phases, and then the hybrid logic dynamic fault model is used to distinguish the power components from the inner and outer parts of the bridge arm. This method does not need to add additional sensors, requires little calculation of fault location, and avoids the influence of load dependence on the selection of diagnostic thresholds, so it has a good engineering application prospect.

articleTitle: Coupled Inductor Based Single-Switch Ultrahigh Step-up Hybrid Switched Capacitor Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposed a coupled inductor based single-switch step-up hybrid switched capacitor DC-DC converter with the advantages of continuously adjustable ultrahigh voltage gain, low input current ripple, and potential for high power density. The converter employs a quadratic boost converter (QBC) on the input side to ensure continuous input current, and the first switched-capacitor (SC) cell is implanted inside it, connected by a coupled inductor (CL) to achieve high gain characteristics. The second SC cell is placed on the output side to reduce voltage spikes generated by leakage inductance and further increase the voltage gain. Analysis including operating principle, steady-state key equations derivation, and comparisons are discussed. A prototype is implemented to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Semiconductor Steady-State Junction Temperatures in Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Semiconductor junction temperature is a key factor determining reliability and energy efficiency of power electronic converters. It also contributes directly to thermal management requirements, which impacts both volumetric and gravimetric power densities of power converters. The thermal coupling displayed by multiple semiconductor devices placed on the same heat sink can cause difficulty in the calculation of the steady-state junction temperature of each component. This paper describes a novel method by which the average losses of each individual semiconductor are used to quickly solve for all devices’ steady-state junction temperatures. The technique employs an iterative approach which then in turn only necessitates a single, brief, time-based thermal simulation, thus bolstering execution speed. When compared to the results from PLECS simulation software, the proposed method can accurately determine the steady-state junction temperatures in only 15-20% of the time, and after including the single, short simulation, there is a 30% speed improvement at low switching frequencies.

articleTitle: The Development of SiC Inverter for In-Wheel Motor Driving
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces the development of SiC inverters for driving in-wheel motors. Two motors are connected by gears, and a SiC MOSFET device was used to manufacture an inverter within a limited space to drive the in-wheel motor. The performance of the developed inverter was confirmed through the dynamometer experiment, and the stability was confirmed through the speed control experiment in the two-motor system. The temperature saturation test of the SiC MOSFET was conducted through continuous driving.

articleTitle: Current sensor fault detection and compensation system for wound rotor synchronous motor based on neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The article presents the idea of using an artificial neural network-based fault classification system for the current sensor (CS) faults. The analysis includes a wound rotor synchronous motor drive system designed according to the idea of fault-tolerant control (FTC). Thanks to the use of the CS fault compensation strategy, the drive system ensures continued functionality, even after a failure has occurred. In the article, the simulation part of the implementation of a CS fault classifier is presented. The neural structure aims to determine the damage category (gain change, offset, saturation, open circuit) and localisation (phase A or B). The developed classifier uses the principal structure of a multilayer perceptron (MLP). The assessment of the type of CS fault is based on single samples of the stator phase current signal. The article shows the high precision of the neural-based classifier that uses the information from the mathematical model in the practical implementation of diagnostic systems for wound rotor synchronous machines.

articleTitle: A New Light Load Efficiency Improving Scheme Utilizing SiC-MOSFET Features of Dynamic Gate Drive Threshold Voltage with Smart Driving Design for Phase Shift Full Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A phase shift full bridge (PSFB) power converter is mainstream topology for server power supplies. It is suitable for high power and efficiency application, however, it could not reach zero voltage switching (ZVS) during the light load operation region. In this articles, dynamic gate drive threshold voltage with smart driving design to achieve light load efficiency improving are introduced and adopted into SiC-MOSFET-based PSFB for full load range operation and severe environment. The advantages and disadvantages of this light load efficiency improving scheme is shown to demonstrate its feasibility and comparing to the pre-loading control scheme for loss breakdown analysis.

articleTitle: IGBT Gate Boost Drive Technology for Promoting the Overload Capacity of Traction Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric locomotives and high-speed EMUs need continuous acceleration or emergency braking under some special route operating conditions, at which time the inverter may have short-term overload conditions, and the current flowing through the IGBT will exceed the rated design tolerance. The IGBT loss will increase instantaneously under overload conditions, resulting in an increase in the junction temperature of the power semiconductor device. Large fluctuations in junction temperature can affect the life of the power device. In this paper, a converter IGBT control technology driven by boosting gate voltage was studied. When the IGBT current capacity needs to be increased for a short time, the gate turn-on voltage can be increased to reduce the conduction voltage drop of the IGBT, thereby reducing the loss and temperature rise fluctuation of the IGBT. Firstly, the influence of gate turn-on voltage rise on IGBT conduction voltage drop and IGBT loss were analyzed, and The IGBT drive circuit with gate boost drive technology was designed. Finally, the effectiveness of this design function was verified by actual switching characteristic test.

articleTitle: Optimization of hybrid energy storage system and energy management for aerial vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: To improve the operation efficiency and reduce fuel consumption of the hybrid energy storage system (HESS) in aerial vehicle applications, this paper proposes a modified active hybrid energy storage system construction. An automatic switch is added, such that the modified system can operate in separate or combination modes according to the power demand. In joint operation mode, an optimization-based model predictive control (MPC) energy management strategy (EMS) is designed to allocate the output power of the two energy sources. Simulation analysis and experimental validation are conducted, and results show that compared to the conventional active system, the modified HESS and the EMS improve the operation efficiency and reduce fuel consumption.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization of Smart Apartment Building with Uncertainty in Photovoltaic Output and Load
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Demand-Side Management (DSM) is undergoing a major transition due to changes in the energy landscape, such as the massive introduction of Renewable Energy Sources (RES). Therefore, in this study, we perform robust optimization for a Smart Apartment (SA) model with uncertainty. Robust optimization models uncertain foctors with an uncertainty set and applies an optimization strategy to the worst-case scenario that may actually occur.
