The optimization strategy consists of two stages. The first stage determines the scheduling on the previous day. At this time, deterministic and robust scheduling are determined. Then, in the second stage, the scheduling on the day is determined by generating forecast errors. The power purchase plan determines by the day-ahead scheduling is input in the second stage, and the operation method is changed to minimize the power shortage. As a result, the effectiveness of robust optimization in previous day scheduling is demonstrated.

articleTitle: New Overmodulation Strategy for Traction Motor in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A strategy for the inverter voltage control during the overmodulation operation is presented to practically use for the traction motor in electric vehicles. This strategy prevents performance degradation of current control by linearizing the modified voltage reference by the overmodulation method. In addition, it facilitates the seamless transition to 6-step operation while maintaining the reasonably low total harmonic distortion. Consequently, vibration and acoustic noise associated with overmodulation are reduced, and the discomfort of passengers is mitigated in electric vehicles. The effectiveness of proposed strategy is verified through simulation tests.

articleTitle: Baseline Determination for Drive Cycle Performance Analysis of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The popularity of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) in electric vehicles (EVs) can be attributed to their impressive power and torque density, high-speed capabilities, and quick dynamic response. In contrast, Induction Motors (IMs) are known for their cost-effectiveness, robustness, ease of control, and superior performance at higher speeds. These motors also differ in terms of rotor losses, overload capacities, application, and industry standards. In the context of analyzing the overall performance of electric drives with these machines across various torque-speed operating points, significant computational effort and time are required. To address this, torque-speed performance maps, also known as efficiency maps, are commonly utilized. However, as these maps are primarily constructed for steady-state operation, their reliability in analyzing transient conditions remains uncertain. This paper presents a baseline for the assessment of the confidence in performance analysis using performance map-based approaches compared to time-stepping analysis of dynamic drive cycles. The evaluation is conducted using a laboratory-based PMSM as an example case. Popular drive cycles for modern traction motors are scaled down to match the PMSM specifications for laboratory testing. Efficiency determination of the drive cycle is carried out using analytic, numerical, and experimental approaches, enabling the extension of the findings to the real-world EV applications.

articleTitle: Rotor Intensity Analysis of High-speed Axial Flux PM Machine for Electric Traction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In comparison with the conventional radial flux (RF) machine, higher torque density and axial compactness are the main attraction for the application of axial flux (AF) machine in electric vehicle traction system. The motivation toward higher speed for traction motors comes from the aggressive cost target per unit for mass manufacturing and improving the power density performance. The axial topology creates mechanical challenges including expansion due to high speed, and axially thin builds that affect rotor dynamics. Based on the determined geometric dimensions of the electromagnetic components, a reliable mechanical construction of dual-rotor is developed for AFPM motor in this paper. Finally, the prototype is successfully manufactured and measured, which verifies that the proposed rotor construction is reliable.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies On Drivers Distractions: Investigating the Effects of Distractions on Driving Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Driving hazards encompass a range of factors, such as poor road conditions, weather, and human behavior. They represent a significant threat to the safety of individuals on the road and are very likely one of the leading causes of traffic accidents. These hazards exist alongside well-known risk factors like driving under the influence of drugs, extreme fatigue, drowsiness, and excessive speeding. Impaired driving, which includes behaviors such as drunk or drugged driving, has persistently plagued American roads for many years. It poses an ongoing risk, not only to the impaired driver but also to other road users and the surrounding infrastructure. The primary objective of this paper is to investigate specific forms of distractions that drivers encounter. These distractions encompass activities such as texting or using a mobile device, eating, conversing with passengers, and paying attention to advertising signs along the roadside. The research aims to understand how each of these distractions affects a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely. In essence, this chapter delves into the various ways in which these distractions can compromise a driver's attention and, consequently, impact road safety.

articleTitle: Radial Force Suppression Method Using A Redundant Degrees of Freedom of Double-star PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a vibration suppression method for double-winding PMSM drive with double three-phase inverter to reduce the vibration of electrical power steering motor. Multiplexing the windings to improve reliability increases the control flexibility and adds redundant degrees of freedom compared to general three-phase PMSM. The redundant degrees of freedom are noted and used to reduce radial force that causes vibration of motor. In this paper, the relationship between the radial force that is cause of vibration and the harmonic current is investigated for the purpose of suppressing the vibration generated from the double-star permanent magnet synchronous motor. Applying harmonic currents of additional degrees of freedom on synchronous frames acts on radial forces of variable orders. Experimental validation shows a 74.7 % reduction in 12th order radial acceleration and a 57.3 % reduction in 4th order radial acceleration.

articleTitle: Adjustable Field PMSM with Rotary Transformer Using Zero-Phase Current and Armature Coil-End
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper describes a new adjustable field permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). There are two types of synchronous motors: one is an electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM), and the other is the PMSM. The EESM can achieve an expansive driving range because the field energy can freely be controlled by brushes, slip rings, and field winding. On the other hand, the PMSM has advantages in efficiency and small motor volume because the recent PM has a high energy density. Against these, the proposed motor has both the field winding and the PM, enabling high-efficiency drive over a wide range. In addition, the proposed motor can receive the field energy wirelessly using special armature coil-ends and a zero-phase current. Therefore, mechanical contacts such as brushes or slip rings can be eliminated. This paper explains the proposed motor’s principles and essential operation characteristics through several computer simulations with a finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Design and Characteristic analysis for the Hybrid Excitation Doubly Salient Generator with Separated Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In response to the increasing power demands of on-board electrical appliances within Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs) and the need for consistent output voltage across a wide range of speeds, this paper introduces an innovative Hybrid Excitation Doubly Salient Generator with Separate Windings (HEDSGSW) structure. The proposed design offers numerous advantages, including simplicity, high reliability, exceptional power density, and consistent output performance. This paper commences with a comprehensive exploration of the electromagnetic structure and the operational magnetic circuit of the high-efficiency double convex pole generator featuring a parallel magnetic circuit structure. Subsequently, it presents a meticulous motor design methodology tailored to the technical requirements and design principles governing this groundbreaking generator. To optimize the motor for enhanced output power and efficiency, this paper conducts a thorough analysis of both stator and rotor structures, focusing on parameter optimization. Furthermore, it synthesizes the impact of each structural parameter on motor performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Active Axial Magnetic Suspension Regulation for a Unsymmetrical Single-Drive Bearingless Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the feasibility of achieving a stable axial magnetic suspension system for a single-drive bearingless motor active positioning on one axis. The proposed bearingless motor has an unsymmetrical structure and high torque density, resulting in highly unstable axial stiffness, making it challenging to achieve a stable axial magnetic suspension of the rotor. The key parameter of the motor is obtained using the FEA analysis platform to analyze the axial magnetic suspension. The study then analyzes the stable magnetic suspension using the MATLAB platform. The study found that the proposed motor can achieve a stable magnetic suspension using a proportional integral derivative (PID) controller with an appropriate second-order cutoff frequency, despite its unsymmetrical structure and highly unstable axial stiffness.

articleTitle: Deep reinforcement learning method for energy management in fast charging station
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) fast charging stations often experience high peak charging loads and strong fluctuations. Therefore, developing an energy management strategy for the energy storage system is crucial to improve load characteristics and reduce peak power. Addressing these challenges, this paper proposes a fast-charging station energy management strategy based on deep reinforcement learning. Firstly, the load characteristics of the charging station are analyzed. Subsequently, a mathematical optimization model is established, aiming to minimize the daily electricity purchase cost of the fast charging station while considering peak power reduction as a constraint. The control strategy is designed using a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. To validate the efficacy of the proposed deep reinforcement learning control strategy, a case study is conducted. The results demonstrate the significant reduction in peak load power, which validates the efficacy of the strategy.

articleTitle: Rotor Electrical Fault Detection in Induction Generators Considering Low-Frequency Oscillations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The induction generator in wind turbine application is subjected to fluctuations caused by polluted grid, tower shadow, and wind speed variations. The oscillations introduced by the mentioned factors especially the low frequency ones make the fault detection in induction generator difficult. In this paper, a model-based technique using the Unscented Kalman filter is proposed for rotor electrical fault detection of a wound rotor induction generator in wind turbine applications. The proper model of induction machine, and the proper measurements and states are introduced, and the corrections need to be considered in calculations are presented. The per-unit calculation makes the algorithm setting easier than the case of using real values. Several scenarios consisting of distorted grid voltage, tower shadow effect, variable wind speed, grid-connected and islanded mode, and low speed operations are studied. The fault detection is assessed thoroughly in the aforementioned conditions by means of simulations. The experimental results prove the effectivity of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Design and Comparison of High-speeds PMSM and IM for Aircraft Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The recent increase in aircraft electrical energy requirements leads to investigate more efficient topologies for on-board electrical generation. This paper present analytical models for the electromagnetic and mechanical design of a PMSM and an IM operating at high-speed levels. The designed machines will be compared in order to study the best solution mainly regarding power density for the application.

articleTitle: Hybrid Learning Model-Based Inter-turn Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper investigates a novel model framework that integrates supervised and unsupervised learning. Based on U-shaped network(U-net) and stacked autoencoder model (SAE), we propose a hybrid model for permanent magnet motor (PMSM) inter-turn fault diagnosis. Generally, small deep networks cannot satisfy complex diagnosis requirements, and larger scale network with high complexity is adverse to use in occasions with low computational resource. the proposed model uses unsupervised learning to assist network parameter optimisation, which makes the small supervised model prone to find the best performance parameters. In this paper, the verification of the proposed model is verified by the 3-phase current data set of PMSM collected under different loads.

articleTitle: A non-cascaded control strategy based on line-constrained EMPC for IPMSMs drive
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper utilizes the constraint handling capability of Explicit Model Predictive Control (EMPC) to propose a technique for non-cascaded line-constrained EMPC applicable to Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (IPMSMs). Owing to its multi-input multi-output structure, it is possible to utilize EMPC to construct a fast-responding, structurally simple non-cascade controller. However, it is challenging to implement non-cascade EMPC algorithms with extended model dimensions on embedded devices due to the memory consumption and execution efficiency issues of traditional EMPC. To address this issue, this paper proposes a solution based on Line-constrained EMPC. By reconfiguring the constraints of the nonlinear EMPC controller into linear constraints, the execution efficiency of the algorithm is significantly improved and memory consumption is reduced, enabling its implementation on embedded devices. The correctness of the algorithm was verified through experimentation.

articleTitle: Magnetic-thermal-solid coupling analysis of V-shaped outer rotor vernier in-wheel motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The hub motor often has a high temperature rise due to the narrow working space and the untimely heat dissipation caused by the loss, which affects the working efficiency of the motor. Aiming at this problem, the temperature rise characteristics and thermal deformation of the hub motor are analyzed. Firstly, a V-type permanent magnet vernier motor with outer rotor is proposed. It is calculated how much the motor will lose under various working situations, and the temperature rise of the motor under different working conditions is analyzed. Through the thermal-solid coupling method, the motor deformation of the motor after a period of rated work is observed. Finally, a permanent magnet motor prototype is used for temperature rise test to verify the accuracy of the temperature field analysis method. The experimental findings demonstrate that the mistake between the temperature rise test and the simulation experiment is 3.8 %, which can prove the accuracy of the magneto-thermal two-way coupling test method.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Eddy Current Speed Sensors for Rotating Speed Measurement of Iron Shafts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A comparative study of two rotational eddy current speed sensors is presented for sensitivity and susceptibility assessment against shaft material properties. The sensors have different coil configurations, with one excitation coil and two antiserially connected pickup coils. The performance of two sensors is compared and evaluated with two iron shafts with different materials shielded by an aluminum shell. The theoretical study of two sensors is performed using the 2D analytical method and the 3D finite element method. The eddy current sensors are measured for a speed range of ±3000 rpm and 500 Hz. The evaluation of eddy current sensors performance for higher speeds is also presented.

articleTitle: A New Discontinuous PWM Method Based on Neutral-Point Voltage Balancing and Low CMV for Single-Phase Three-Level Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a new discontinuous PWM method to reduce the minimum number of switchings without loss of control neutral point (NP) voltage balancing for single-phase three-level inverters by considering a single-phase three-level full-bridge inverter as same a two-phase matrix converter and switching sequence concepts of the matrix converter are modified to this inverter. The research results reveal that the proposed PWM method can control the minimum number of switchings and the NP voltage balancing. Also, low common-mode voltage (CMV) can be achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis of External Excited Synchronous Machine for EV Traction Considering Maximum Efficiency Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper deals with the comparison of efficiency maps according to the initial design and control method of EESM for driving electric vehicles. In order to verify the effect of the maximum efficiency control proposed in this paper, an initial EESM model that satisfies the performance of the existing IPMSM is designed. Then, the efficiency map is calculated by applying the Maximum torque per Ampere control and maximum efficiency control to the d- and q-axis equivalent circuit analysis, respectively. The effectiveness of the maximum efficiency control presented in this paper was verified by comparing the efficiency maps for each control method.

articleTitle: Bus-bar Design for Silicon-Carbide based Medium Voltage Full-bridge Based Converter Topologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The advancement in SiC technology is helping to achieve high efficiency and high power density in medium voltage high power applications. SiC comes with various challenges due to fast switching transients. Medium voltage converters are used for various applications. Most of the dc-dc isolated high-power converters are based on full-bridge topologies. In these topologies, bus bar design plays a critical role in the performance for the medium voltage devices. Most critical aspect in medium voltage device based converter is isolation requirement between positive and negative dc-link bus bars. This paper deals with bus bar design of medium voltage device based full bridge topology. Effects of non-ideality of bus-bar is analyzed with spice simulations. Various configurations of bus-bar arrangements are discussed and compared using FEM simulations. One suitable configuration is implemented and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Resonant Switched Capacitor Converter with Conduction Losses Reduction by Generating Trapezoidal wave current for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: EV battery voltages are increasing from the conventional 400 V to 800 V. To fully utilize existing 400 V chargers for such high-voltage batteries, an on-board boost converter with a step-up conversion ratio of 2.0 is required. Resonant switched capacitor converters (RSCCs) are known as the best topology to reduce circuit volume. However, a rms current of the resonant sinusoidal wave is larger than their input current, leading to increased conduction losses. This paper proposes a PWM modulated RSCC to reduce conduction losses by generating the trapezoidal wave current. In addition, the trapezoidal wave current can further reduce current stresses due to reducing current amplitude. A prototype verification test demonstrated the reduction of conduction losses by approximately 12% compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: On-Board Integrated Charger Based on Open-End Winding AC Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents an on-board integrated charger for electric vehicles (EVs) based on an open-end winding AC machine. To reduce weight, volume, and costs, including additional space area in EVs, the main component of the traction system is utilized as a part of the charger system, i.e., the wound rotor open-end winding AC machine fed by a dual converter with a single battery source. In charging operation, the rotor winding side of the AC machine is at standstill and reconfigured through magnetic contactors to interface with the three-phase utility grid, whereas the stator winding side is still connected to the converters. It performs as a transformer isolated by itself. On the other hand, the rotor windings are shorted together for the driving operation. Besides, the charger system assists the stability of the utility grid by consuming constant power, absorbing maximum power rated at 22 kW. To enhance excellent control, the modulation strategy of the dual converter is determined by means of different phase angles of 120° As a result, the differential-mode voltage problem is suppressed. The simulation results are validated to confirm the performance of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Design of Horizontally Aligned Six-Plate Capacitive Power Transfer for EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Researchers have shown interest in wireless power transfer (WPT) technology for EV charging due to its salient features of safety, convenience, and the possibility of opportunity charging. Inductive power transfer (IPT) has been used commonly; however, it has an issue of misalignment intolerance and high cost. Alternatively, the capacitive power transfer (CPT)-based charging systems can be utilized, which offers better misalignment, lower cost, and lightweight. However, it displays lesser power density and efficiency than IPT systems. Therefore, the design of the CPT coupler is crucial to improving the CPT system performance. This paper presents a group of horizontally aligned six-plate couplers to achieve higher power transfer capability with better electric field shielding. The performance of these CPT couplers is holistically evaluated to get the best CPT coupler structure through finite-element analysis (FEA) in ANSYS-MAXWELL software. The results shows that HCC3 coupler performs better in terms of electric field emissions and HCC1 is suitable for high power EV charging.

articleTitle: Improved SRF-PLL Based Position Sensorless BLDC Motor in EV Drive With DC Offset Rejection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this paper a new position sensorless approach for brushless direct current (BLDC) motor drive using synchronous reference frame (SRF)-PLL method is utilized with zero DC offset. The rotor angular position is estimated with SRF-PLL from the terminal voltages of the motor. It is found that for a BLDC motor, the phase of the terminal voltage defines the rotor position. Therefore, the conventional back EMF ZCP-based method can be replaced by SRF-PLL for position estimation, which offers good accuracy, enhanced filtering, and robustness under the DC link voltage variation. The estimated position is converted to virtual commutation signals. The presence of a DC offset in the input of PLL causes oscillation in fundamental frequency, which adds error in position estimation. This error degrades motor performance with additional current and torque ripples. Therefore, a DC offset rejection technique is added with a conventional SRF-PLL for further improvement in motor drive performance for EV applications.

articleTitle: Alternative Control Methodology of Grid-Supporting Grid-Forming Power Converter with a Proportional Complex-Vector Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: An alternative control methodology for a grid-supporting grid-forming (GSGFm) power converter operating within a synchronous rotating reference frame (SRRF) is developed in this research. The proposed methodology combines a proportional (P)-based controller with a complex-vector (CV) controller to effectively mitigate distortions. The cascade voltage and current control structure employed in this methodology leverages a two-proportional controller to precisely regulate the dq-components of voltage and currents. Additionally, a two-complex-vector controller is utilized to attenuate periodic disturbances that may arise during operation. Experimental results have been conducted to evaluate and validate the performance of the suggested methodology. The obtained results provide empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: Torque ripple Reduction of IPMSM Applying 2-step Magnetic skew
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper concentrates on designing a motor utilizing a two-step magnetic skew shape and compares its torque ripple with those of a motor employing mechanical step skew and a non-skew model. In the magnetic step skew method, permanent magnets are identically positioned in both the first and second steps of the motor; however, the bridge shape is asymmetrically designed. By laminating the first and second steps in opposite directions, the magnetic resistance can be effectively altered. This approach has confirmed a reduction in torque ripple and, unlike the mechanical step skew method, an increase in average torque. The non-skew, magnetic step skew, and mechanical step skew models were analyzed and compared for torque ripple using 2-D Finite Element Analysis (2-D FEA).

articleTitle: Development of an Omni-directional Human-friendly Mobility Platform for Industrial Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A mobility platform has been widely used in many applications due to its load and transportation capacity. Movement capability, position estimation, and human interaction functions are essential in the mobility platform. This paper proposed a mobility platform to apply for intelligent factories or parcel distribution warehouses. In the mobility platform, a novel power train structure with a drive-suspension integrated module is proposed to enhance the load capability and drive in arbitrary direction movement. Consequently, the mobility platform can be modified to treat the various sizes of load objects. Moreover, the paper presents the sensor fusion algorithm that uses low-cost sensors to estimate the position of the mobility platform. Additionally, the user-friendly motion to intuitively maneuver the mobility system is a particular function compared with conventional mobility platforms. Several experiment results verify the proposed algorithms, including position control in a given path, position measurement, and one-hand maneuvering test.

articleTitle: Power Angle Control of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner in Railway Electrification System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents the load reactive power demand sharing strategy based on power angle control (PAC) method for the unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) in the railway electrification system. This work focuses on performance of reference signal generation for UPQC. Therefore, to clearly investigate its performance, the series active power filter (series APF) and shunt active power filter (shunt APF) are represented by ideal voltage sources and ideal current sources, respectively. The testing results by the processor-in-the-loop (PIL) technique on an eZdsp<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> F28335 board and the MATLAB/Simulink program confirm that the proposed strategy can share the balanced load reactive power compensations between the series APF and the shunt APF. The harmonic current mitigation, power factor correction, and voltage variations (sag/swell) compensation in the railway electrification system can also be achieved using the UPQC with the proposed strategy. The performance indices for the power quality improvement can also be kept within the IEEE Standard 519 and the IEEE Standard 141.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Spraying F-500 Substance of Twin-Fluid Nozzle on Suppression for Lithium-Ion Battery Cell Fires
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The use of lithium-ion batteries has rapidly increased especially in applications such as electric vehicles, data centers, and energy storage systems. Since this demand has risen due to the global attempt to reduce carbon emissions and it is important to diminish any drawbacks related to Lithium-ion batteries. One of the major challenges that lithium-ion batteries face is its potential to induce fire. Introducing a fire suppression system for lithium-ion batteries could be identified as a suitable option to overcome this obstacle. This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of suppressing thermal runaway (TR) in Lithium Nickel Cobalt Aluminum Oxide (NCA) batteries at a 100% state of charge (SOC). A twin-fluid nozzle combining nitrogen gas and F-500 liquid substance was applied at an angle of 60 degrees to the horizontal axis. Tests were performed differentiating the nitrogen gas flow rate (1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 CFM) for spray injection onto the battery surface at temperatures of 160, 165, 170, and 180 °C. Spray durations were selected as 5, 10, and 15 s. Results showed as the spray duration increases from 5 to 10 and 15 s, the suppression effectiveness improves 23.6%, 41.4%, and 68.6% respectively. Additionally, it was observed that the system achieved its highest suppression effectiveness, reaching 78.2%, when the battery surface temperature at the start of injection was at 160 °C.

articleTitle: Electric Motor Drive Toolkits using Digital Signal Processor (DSP) based on Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) design and development approach for an Electric Vehicle (EV) controller, specifically tailored to academic environments. The system comprises a Digital Signal Processor (DSP), an Intelligent Power Module (IPM) inverter, and a low-power Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor. Algorithm development and simulation are carried out using MATLAB Simulink. The HIL technique facilitates a safe hands-on learning experience by accurately replicating vital functionalities of real EV systems. The proposed affordable EV controller solution enables practical learning opportunities while maintaining optimal safety and performance standards. This research contributes to the cultivation of skilled engineers well-prepared to address the evolving challenges in the expanding EV industry.

articleTitle: A New Fourier Modeling Method for Switched Reluctance Motors Based on Small Sample Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately establish the switched reluctance motor (SRM) model, this paper proposes a new method for Fourier modeling of switched reluctance motor based on small sample data. First, the flux data of four special positions are measured by the torque balance method, and then the data of four curves are used to obtain the fifth flux curve. The fifth-order Fourier model can be built using the obtained data. Finally, the accuracy of the model of the proposed method is verified on the hardware platform. The experimental results show that the modeling accuracy of the proposed method is higher than that of the conventional method under current chopping control (CCC) and angular position control (APC), and the modeling is simpler and faster without additional clamping devices.

articleTitle: Distributed control of electric vehicle clusters for user-based power scheduling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) in the power system has raised concerns regarding the management of charging sessions to prevent systems from overloading. This paper proposes a distributed control method of EV clusters that enables controllers to make decisions independently, using only commonly broadcasted signals. Additionally, the method also includes a user-based power scheduling mechanism that prioritizes EVs based on their respective energy needs and time availability. A power-constrained system is considered for the case studies, where the system is only capable of charging one EV with maximum power. Simulation results demonstrate that the system effectively accommodates and schedules multiple EVs to charge simultaneously in a restricted environment without compromising user satisfaction. In instances of communication loss, the system demonstrates the capability to sustain the charging process through resource reallocation. The method is characterized by its distributed and autonomous nature, which ensures both robustness and effective operation.

articleTitle: Baseline Determination for Drive Cycle Performance Analysis of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The rise of electric vehicles (EVs) highlights the importance of performance analysis and efficient motor selection, including Induction Motors (IMs). Induction motors provide enhanced efficiency in the flux-weakening region, leading to increased ranges for EVs, and offering robustness and cost-effectiveness compared to permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). However, it is important to note that IMs experience rotor cage losses at both high and low speeds. Accurate efficiency mapping plays a vital role in facilitating the design of EV motors. Efficiency analysis of dynamic drive cycle operating points is crucial for evaluating vehicle motors. This paper presents a baseline assessment for performance analysis, focusing on enhancing efficiency map accuracy through comprehensive drive cycle analysis using a combination of experiments, analytic modeling, and numerical simulations on a laboratory-scale IM. Analytic and numerical models are created and performance plots are studied for a particular drive cycle covering a wide range of operating points. A dedicated test-rig is set up to examine the transient behavior of the motor during drive cycles, allowing for a thorough analysis of its dynamic performance. The research findings can be generalized to benefit real EV motors.

articleTitle: Study of New Rotor Structure of Variable Flux Motor with Drawable Stator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this study, we focus on a variable flux motor with a drawable stator, in which the magnetic flux is controlled by drawing out its stator and changing the facing area between its rotor and stator. First, we describe the characteristics and problems of a variable flux motor with a drawable stator. Second, we propose a new rotor structure that consists of two types of rotors with different characteristics. Finally, we conclude that the new rotor achieves high efficiency and high power in both low- and high-speed areas.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Torque Control of an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted maximum-torque-per-ampere control of an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM). For torque control of an IPMSM, the optimum current trajectories are calculated. The current components are determined such that the magnitude of the current vector is minimized for a reference torque. Especially in the field weakening range, this results in nonlinear equations that have to be solved, which is why the current components are often calculated offline and stored discretely in look-up tables (LUTs). Due to the discrete storage of data, interpolation is performed for data not included in the LUT, resulting in interpolation errors. In this work, these LUTs are replaced by neural networks, minimizing this interpolation error. In addition to a significantly improved interpolation accuracy, the required memory space on a microcontroller is also minimized.

articleTitle: Time Based Adaptive Scheme for SiC-Based Totem Pole PFC and FBLLC Stage for Portable EV Charger Design with G2V/V2X Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The design of totem pole PFC (Power Factor Correction) stage for EV charger needs wide variation in switching frequency. This is due to wide regulation in an intermediate DC link. This leads to lose of ZVS margin. For this, an analytical model of totem pole PFC stage is designed. It is based on high frequency PWM turn-off current. This sensed quantity is used to extend ZVS margin. This control degree of freedom regulates needed reactive energy to achieve ZVS over any variation in the DC link voltage reference. This action reduces complete range of switching frequency. The ZVS margin in FBLLC stage is controlled by controlling a shift of rising edge need to discharge the incoming MOSFET. It is needed at light loading scenario when reactive energy is not sufficient to achieve ZVS. It is designed based on mathematical expression presented. A hybrid intermediate DC link approach is utilized for wide battery voltage. A modified pre-filtering stage with adaptive fixed frequency SOGI is utilized for grid angle estimation under worst grid scenarios. A 3.3 kW system is designed to validate designed control over multiple grid and loading scenarios.

articleTitle: Coordinated Charging and Discharging of Electric Vehicles With Multiple Trips
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The proliferation of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), especially taking vehicle to grid (V2G) into consideration, imposes operational challenges to the existing power systems and thereby calls for effective coordinated load control method. From the perspective of PEV owners, coordinated charging and discharging of PEVs can reduce their energy purchase cost and V2G enables them to participate in the energy and ancillary markets. In this paper, the aggregate PEV charging and discharging power and energy models are built first considering the trip chains of PEVs within a whole day. A coordinated PEV charging and discharging strategy is then proposed to reduce the total charging cost and promote the integration of PEVs and distributed generation (DG). Simulation results show that the proposed charging and discharging strategy for PEVs can effectively reduce the costs for PEV users, promote the integration of photovoltaic (PV) generation, and smooth the total load profile.

articleTitle: Adaptive integral-type second-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode control of permanent magnet linear synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: An adaptive integral-type second-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode control approach is proposed to address the stability concerns in the control system of a permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM), which is susceptible to uncertainties and load disturbances. This method utilizes second-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode control based on sliding mode control theory to ensure finite time convergence of the system. An integral second-order sliding mode surface is defined to eliminate the steady-state error caused by uncertain factors. Additionally, an adaptive mechanism estimates the upper bound of uncertainties, resulting in a parameter-turning terminal sliding mode tracking controller that improves the system's anti-interference capability and reduces the sliding mode chattering phenomenon. The proposed adaptive integral-type second-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller is developed without assuming prior knowledge of the upper bound of uncertainties. Experimental results demonstrate superior antiinterference capability, position tracking accuracy, convergence speed, and effective chattering suppression compared to traditional second-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode control methods that rely on assumed upper bounds of uncertainties.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of Dual Movers for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In this study, a novel type of control system for the coordinated motion of dual movers is proposed, which is based on the moving magnet Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor (PMSLM). Compared with the traditional control system that adopts master-slave control or deviation coupling control algorithm, the control system proposed in this study is powered by only one power module to realize the coordinated movement of dual movers, which reduces a set of power modules. It is verified by simulation that the dual movers can move synchronously with a controllable distance.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic System Realizing Reduced Power Rating and Circuit Volume in Combination with Partially Connected Converter and Differential Power Processing Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In photovoltaic (PV) systems consisting of multiple PV panels connected in series, conventional converters require a large power rating due to handling the power generated by all panels, resulting in increased circuit volume. A PV system in which a converter is partially connected to series-connected panels has been proposed to reduce power rating. However, a partially connected converter triggers the mismatch in panel characteristics, leading to decreased energy yield. This paper proposes a novel PV system in combination with the partially connected converter and a differential power processing (DPP) converter that can unify panel voltage. By utilizing the DPP converter that is gaining attention as a solution to partial shading issues, the proposed system realizes not only eliminating panel voltage imbalance and enhancing energy yield but also a reduction in power rating and circuit volume by the partially connected converter. Theoretical analysis of a PV string comprising four series panels demonstrated that in addition to the power rating reduction of up to 58%. The performance evaluation of the conventional system and the proposed system in terms of circuit volume suggests that the proposed system achieves circuit miniaturization than the conventional system. Experimental verification of PV systems using prototypes demonstrated that in addition to energy yield enhancement of 12% by the DPP converter, the proposed system achieved an overall efficiency of up to 98%.

articleTitle: Research on Magnetic Circuit and Electromagnetic Performance of Combined-Pole Less-Rare-Earth Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machine Used for Fully Electric Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The combined-pole less-rare-earth permanent-magnet synchronous machine (CP-LRE-PMSM) has a series of advantages, such as better sinusoidal air-gap field, reduced reliance on rare-earth permanent-magnet materials. and lower cost. This paper firstly founds CP-LRE-PMSM’s equivalent magnetic circuit model, then the calculation formulas of air-gap field are deduced, meanwhile the model accuracy is examined by finite element analysis (FEA). After that, based on machine performance requirements used for fully electric unmanned aerial vehicle (FE-UAV), the electromagnetic performance of CP-LRE-PMSM is analyzed. The total harmonics distortion (THD) and fundamental component of air-gap field versus permanent magnet width, permanent magnet thickness and flux-barrier position angle are studied, respectively. The torque characteristics and the machine efficiency map are investigated, which provides the reference for theoretical analysis and design of the CP-LRE-PMSM

articleTitle: Thermal Modeling of the Slot of an Electric Machine Considering Position Deviations of Individual Conductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Thermal modeling of the slots in electric machines is of great importance for the development of highly utilized machines. A novel method was developed, which enables the calculation of individual conductor temperatures in a filled slot. Analytical equations from potential theory are used to keep the computation time low compared to numerical methods. An underlying variation of the conductor arrangements allows for improved accuracy with respect to the realistic modeling of the conductor arrangement in the slot. The results of the method are verified by means of finite element analysis and show high agreement.

articleTitle: Half Bridge DC-DC Converter Based Li/Ion Charger Fed By Hysteresis Controlled PFC SEPIC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Li/Ion battery charger study for electrical vehicle using half bridge converter is presented herein. Besides half bridge converter is tied to the grid by single phase PFC SEPIC converter to increase PF and decrease THD of grid current through LCL filter. Further, the PFC converter has hysteresis current control. Matlab/Simulink simulation is used for the study. By means of the simulation, Li/Ion state of charge and voltage are measured to prove that the Li/Ion is charged. Also, THD of grid current is obtained as 3.42 % and PF is measured as 0.999. It is validated that THD is decreased below the limit in the standards and PF is increased nearly to the unity.

articleTitle: Interleaved multi-port converter with single inductor for photovoltaic energy storage systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: In traditional photovoltaic (PV) systems with batteries, the complexity and size of the system become challenges because separate converters are required to control the PV panels and the batteries. Although conventional multi-port converters (MPCs) can reduce the number of components by integrating multiple converters into one, the multiple inductors cause increased losses and reduced efficiency. This paper proposes an MPC that integrates multiple converters into one to simplify and downsize the PV systems. By cascading two converters, the circuit is simplified because it consists of only one inductor. In addition, the interleaved operation reduces the current ripple of the inductor and makes it smaller. A 300-W prototype is implemented, and the theoretical analysis is validated by the experimental results.

articleTitle: A Novel Wireless Power Transfer System with Reflex-Charging and Cell-Balancing Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces a wireless power transfer (WPT) system that incorporates energy recycling capabilities at the receiver (Rx) for the purpose of reflex-charging and cell-balancing in battery strings. The proposed system comprises a non-dissipative active energy buffer that stores and releases energy via a phase-shifted half-bridge rectifier (PSHBR) and an inductor. This arrangement enables reflex charging and active balancing among the batteries. The reflex-charging mechanism not only lowers the internal resistance of the batteries but also accelerates the charging process while minimizing temperature elevation. This paper provides system descriptions, circuit operation details, and circuit numerical analysis to support the proposed concept. The results obtained from these analyses validate the effectiveness of the proposed concept, demonstrating that the system achieves maximum power efficiency of 90.2%, and enhances battery charging performance in terms of speed and reliability.

articleTitle: Estimation of Permanent Magnet Demagnetization Using MRAS with no Sensitivity to Winding Resistance of IPM Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Accurate parameter estimation is crucial for the optimal operation and control of interior permanent magnet (IPM) motors. This study proposes a parameter identification technique for permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage utilizing a hybrid approach, combining a finite element method (FEM)-based 3D-Inductance map and a model reference adaptive system (MRAS) based on instantaneous reactive power. Considering the cross-coupling effect, the objective is to improve the control output performance by reducing transient response errors and conducting PM flux linkage identification under magnetic saturation. The proposed parameter estimation method is robust and fast to adapt to dynamic motor operation and, simultaneously, online and able to determine the PM flux linkage. The FEM-based map provides a comprehensive model of the IPM motor by considering the spatial variation of inductances across the motor cross-section. The MRAS utilizes the reactive power component of the motor to estimate the PM flux linkage by comparing the measured and estimated instantaneous reactive power. By comparing the output of the reference model with the actual motor response, the MRAS algorithm adapts the estimated parameters to minimize the error between the two. This study proposed the reactive power component as it has no sensitivity with resistance. So, the impact of motor operation, which lead to heat production and variation of winding resistance, will not affect the proposed method. As a result, the parameter mismatches due to PM demagnetization and magnetic saturation are significantly reduced.

articleTitle: State of Energy Based Secondary Control Scheme of Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper proposes a secondary control scheme for virtual power plant based on the state of energy. The scheme is to operate various energy systems that interact within the domains of electrical, gas, and heat energy integration. Initially, the state of energy is determined by analyzing the characteristics of various energy sectors, including water electrolysis devices, fuel cells, battery energy storage systems, and heat pumps, among others. Subsequently, a secondary control scheme for the virtual power plant is designed integrating reserves calculated from the state of energy. This scheme aims to provide integration strategies for the energy sectors, offering ancillary services to aid in power grid stabilization. The effectiveness of the proposed control method has been validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Analytically Optimized Asymmetric Coupler Design for Wireless Drone Charging with Receiver-side Weight Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical design optimization of an asymmetric coupler based inductive wireless drone charging system with a receiver-side weight constraint arising from the payload limit of the drone. To avoid time-consuming finite element analysis, the geometrical parameters of the circular planar coils are analytically designed to maximize coil-to-coil efficiency while achieving the target mutual inductance between the coils and adhering to a maximum allowed weight on the receiver side. The proposed analytical optimization shows that an asymmetric coupler results in an enhanced coil-to-coil efficiency compared to the conventional symmetric coupler while also reducing the weight of the receiver coil. A 85-kHz 4.5-cm air-gap 100-W experimental prototype of a wireless drone charging system having the proposed asymmetric coupler is built and tested. The prototype achieves a coil-to-coil efficiency of 91.3% while limiting the receiver coil weight below the drone’s payload limit. Furthermore, the proposed efficiency benefit is experimentally validated by comparing the performance of this asymmetric coupler based prototype with that comprising a symmetric coupler for the same system specifications.

articleTitle: Deep Transfer Learning-Based Demagnetization Analysis for Linear Oscillating Actuator Considering Circumferential Segmented Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The linear oscillating actuator (LOA) achieves high efficiency and features a simple mechanical structure because it doesn’t require the conversion of rotational motion into linear motion. Therefore, the LOA is an appealing option for devices such as compressors, linear pump and automobile active suspension due to its high efficiency and power density. The stability of permanent magnets (PMs) can be impacted by different factors such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and other external influences. In more severe cases, these factors can result in the occurrence of irreversible demagnetization, causing permanent damage to the magnetic properties of the PM. The irreversible demagnetization of permanent magnets impacts the electromagnetic functionality of the LOA, making it necessary to account for it during the design stage. However, the intricate configuration of the LOA such as divided outer stator and PMs diminishes accuracy of the 2-D finite element analysis (FEA). Despite its high computational cost for calculating accurate demagnetization ratio (DR), 3-D FEA is essential. Thus, we propose a demagnetization analysis based on transfer learning (TL) to reduce the computational cost associated with accurately calculating the 3-D FEA-based DR. This approach takes into account the permeance in the stator core and circumferential leakage flux. With TL, the parameters of pre-trained models learned from a source dataset in different but similar domains are transferred to learn the target dataset and effectively enhance the performance of neural network. The TL is conducted with a substantial dataset from 2-D FEA-based demagnetization ratio (DR) anda limited dataset from 3-D FEA-based DR. TL is a cognitive learning approach that utilizes knowledge acquired from a source task to enhance learning in a related but different target task were compared.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Method for Charging Station Management and Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and the corresponding renewable energy-based charging stations (CSs) are rapidly gaining popularity as an effective solution for environmental protection. However, the increasing adoption of EVs and CSs can lead to load fluctuations and pose safety risks to the grid. To address this issue and develop a practical management strategy for CSs, we propose a load-constraint hierarchical deep reinforcement learning approach. Our method aims to achieve two main objectives: 1) maximize the total profit and balance the load for CSs, taking into account the unpredictable behavior of EV users; and 2) separate pricing and charging scheduling actions to enhance training efficiency. We conducted experiments using real data, and the results validate the effectiveness of our algorithm in achieving load balancing and maximizing profits for CSs.

articleTitle: Investigation on Structures of Axial Gap Type Magnetic Multiple Spur Gear for In-Wheel Motor System of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: A novel drive system using Magnetic Multiple Spur Gear (MMSG) and multiple high-speed motors is characterized by small size, lightweight, and high efficiency even at high-speed region, it is expected to apply to in-wheel motor systems. However, there is a risk of contact between the rotors when applied to in-wheel motor system. In this study, a novel axial-gap MMSG is proposed to solve this problem, stabilize the air gap between the high-speed and low-speed rotors, and effectively utilize the magnets, and its performance is evaluated by finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Massive Connectivity Provision for V2X Based on Low Power IoT Standards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Intelligent vehicles rely on ubiquitous sensing of the environment, where a large number of devices are deployed to collect data needed such that vehicle to everything (V2X) is enabled. To this end, simultaneous massive connectivity is required to render intelligent transportation, which is the main challenge in V2X network. This paper proposed using multiple-input multiple-output non-orthogonal multiple access (MIMO-NOMA) to provide massive connectivity for V2X network, where the access point equipped with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> antennas to serve K devices simultaneously over a single time-frequency resource block (i.e., wireless channel). This setup leads to the development of MIMO-NOMA based on low power internet of things (IoT) standards such as IEEE 802.15.4 series, which means provision of V2X massive connectivity is easily enabled using off-the-shelf equipment. The analysis and numerical results confirm that the proposed method outperforms existing peers, while supporting a large number of devices.

articleTitle: DAB Converter Performing Internal AC Heating and Power Transfer Simultaneously for Lithium-Ion Battery in Electronic Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) significantly increased internal resistances at low temperatures, shortening the cruising distances of electric vehicles. Hence, LIBs require to be properly preheated. Internal ac heating techniques utilizing the Joule heat originating from LIB’s internal resistances have been proposed as an efficient heating method. A dual active bridge (DAB) converter integrating the internal ac heating inverter has been proposed. However, using a sinusoidal reference signal, the conventional control strategy cannot perform stable power transfer during internal ac heating. This paper proposes a control strategy to perform stable power transfer and internal ac heating simultaneously by changing the switching patterns every half-cycle of the ac heating current. Experimental results demonstrated that internal ac heating and stable power transfer can perform simultaneously.

articleTitle: Comparative study of efficiency improvement with adjustable DC-link voltage powertrain using DC-DC converter and Quasi-Z-Source inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Adjusting the DC-link voltage in the electric pow-ertrain has proven to be beneficial for enhancing powertrain efficiency. This paper presents a comparative study between two adjustable DC-link voltage powertrain solutions: (1) Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) integrated with a DC-DC converter (VSI+DC-DC) and (2) Quasi-Z-Source Inverter (QZSI). Based on the different operation principles of the two solutions, DC-link voltage adjustment strategies have been proposed to maximize powertrain efficiency over drive cycle operation. With the help of simulation in the PLECS environment, the powertrain losses of the two solutions are examined over the WLTC drive cycle. The results suggest both solutions can achieve significant powertrain loss reduction compared to the conventional powertrain with fixed DC-link voltage. In addition, the QZSI solution sees a 20% higher loss in power electronics than the VSI+DC-DC solution, as the DC-link voltage in the QZSI solution has to be boosted to higher values. Nevertheless, from an overall powertrain perspective, the QZSI solution has only 3% higher powertrain losses compared to the VSI+DC-DC solution, making QZSI remain an attractive alternative for adjustable DC-link powertrain given its advantages such as fewer active switches and improved system reliability.

articleTitle: Design Optimization and Comparative Analysis of Permanent-Magnet Vernier Machines with Single-Winding Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper conducts a comparative study among four permanent-magnet (PM) vernier (PMV) machines with single-winding design, including the surface-mounted PMV (SPMV) machine, the spoke-array PMV (SAPMV) machine, the U-shape consequent-pole PMV (UCPMV) machine, and the dual-stator PMV (DSPMV) machine. The machine topologies and design principles of four PMV machines are introduced, and the underlying reason for the design of the half-slot pitch displacement between two stators in the DSPMV machine is revealed analytically. Then, the multi-objective optimization using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) is carried out among four types of PMV machines, aiming to deliver high performances such as high output torque, high efficiency, high power factor, low PM consumption, and low torque ripple for practical industrial applications. The electromagnetic performances of the optimal designs are comprehensively evaluated using finite-element analysis (FEA). The advantages and disadvantages of each type of PMV machine are summarized, offering valuable insights to researchers in machine type selection.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of Commercial High Energy and High Power Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This work aims to investigate the fundamental characteristics of Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery cells, which are generally distinct by their energy and power capability. The commercial high energy and high power Li-ion battery cells were characterised their physical, electrical and chemical properties. Physical properties, such as geometry and capacity of each cell were measured. Electrical properties, such as internal resistances, power characteristics were also tested. The results on energy and power densities of each battery cell and power-to-energy ratio (P/E ratio) could be simultaneously obtained. The cells were subsequently disassembled in order to characterise their internal properties. The thicknesses of electrodes, separator and current collectors were measured. The morphology of cathode and anode was observed by the scanning electron microscope (SEM) as well as the visible particle size. Chemical analysis was conducted by energy dispersive spectroscopy to identify the chemistry of the electrodes. Finally, all the characteristics measured and obtained were explained in relation with the P/E ratio. It was found that battery cells with high energy tended to have high internal resistances, large particle size of active materials in both cathode and anode. The cells contained the thick cathode and anode and thin current collectors and separator due to the benefit of high amount of energy capacity coatings. Conversely, the battery with high power tended to show the opposite characteristics. The relationship between these properties versus P/E ratio was attempted to develop. It showed a well-correlated result for some extents. However, due to the difference of battery chemistries and different manufacturer, it was still hard to make a strong correlation between the properties and P/E ratio, which need to be more clarified.

articleTitle: Modified Flux Observer based Sensorless PMSM Control for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: The adoption of sensorless rotor position estimation without need for mechanical sensors, represents a prominent solution to effectively enhance robustness and making cost effective without compromising performance. In this paper, a sensorless rotor position finding approach for surface mounted PMSM by modified flux observer (FO) for solar PV array- battery fed lightweight electric vehicle (EV) with feature of regenerative braking is presented. Modified FO approach incorporates an interference observer and a quasi-proportional resonant (QPR) based controller. This new design effectively addresses main challenges encountered in conventional FO methods, offering robustness against the DC offset and integrator issues while maintaining a remarkably simple and streamlined structure. The interference observer (IO) plays a crucial role in eradicating the DC offset and harmonics from flux estimation without introducing any errors into the estimated flux. Furthermore, the utilization of quasi PR feedback control enables elimination of discrepancies between observed and actual current, leading to a harmonics-immune performance. Performance evaluation of the control and topology is done on a 3-kW PMSM based on obtained results.

articleTitle: Ultra-High-Power-Rate PM Motor with Double Stator Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper describes feasibility of a permanent magnet (PM) motor, with a hollow rotor and a double stator structure to achieve high power rate for higher acceleration and deceleration. In the case of a single-stator motor, the rotor must be thicker in the radial direction to take advantage of reluctance torque for higher torque delivery. However, the rotor inertia depends on the radial thickness; hence there is a tradeoff between higher torque generation and lowering the inertia. The double stator motor has two torque-generating surfaces in a radial direction, which not only increases the magnet torque but also makes reluctance torque generation possible because the inner stator can effectively be utilized as a q-axis magnetic circuit even though the thin rotor structure is employed. In the paper, finite element method (FEM) analysis results show that the hollow rotor and double stator structure can achieve an ultra high power rate and extremely higher acceleration and deceleration, which contributes shortened tact time in manufacturing process. In addition, it has also been demonstrated that the inner stator of the double stator structure can efficiently be used as a q-axis magnetic circuit to generate the reluctance torque although the thin rotor shape. Furthermore, the superiority of the proposed double stator motor over the single stator motor for high power rates is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Conversion and Test Results of Slotted to Slotless Brushless DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This study focuses on the conversion process and testing outcomes of a slotted to slotless brushless DC motor. The main objective was to assess the performance characteristics of a newly developed slotless brushless motor derived from a 12-slot/8-pole slotted brushless DC motor. The conversion involved removing the stator core of the existing slotted brushless motor and implementing a new rectangular winding set without a stator core to create a slotless brushless DC motor. The design details of the new three-phase winding for the slotless motor are also presented. Experimental tests were conducted, including rotational speed tests and wind speed tests under different load conditions. The test results demonstrated the proposed slotless brushless DC motor has higher achievable speeds of up to 18 times at the no-load test, a weight reduction of up to 28.5 %, and higher wind velocity of up to 2.5 times compared to the existing slotted brushless DC motor.

articleTitle: A New Switching Pattern to Reduce Common-Mode Voltage for Matrix Converters Based on Minimum Number of Switchings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: From problems with motor shaft voltages, bearing leakage currents, and conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI), this paper proposes a new switching pattern for matrix converters to reduce common-mode voltage by arranging the switching sequence of the unipolar PWM in a carrier-based dipolar modulation. The simulation results reveal that the common-mode voltage can be suppressed by the proposed switching pattern with the minimum number of switchings and a low ripple of output voltages and input currents.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Optimization Method for Active Distribution Network Considering the Regulating Capacity of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Currently, the operation optimization of smart distribution networks with distributed power sources does not fully consider the supply-demand interaction of flexible loads, such as electric vehicles, and cannot systematically solve the operation optimization problem of smart distribution networks. In this paper, a method for optimizing the operation of smart distribution networks considering the regulation capability of electric vehicles is proposed. Firstly, the operational status of the distribution network is obtained through measurement datas. Then, the objective functions of distribution network losses, maximum output of distributed power sources, compensation costs for flexible loads, and incentive load costs are established. Moreover, the constraints of power flow balance, node voltage, output power of distributed power , and maximum flexible load are considered. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is used for optimization calculation of distribution networks. The IEEE 33 node example shows that the regulation ability of flexible loads has been utilized, increasing the output of distributed power sources by 20% and reducing network losses by 30%.

articleTitle: Radiated EMI Reduction and Efficiency Improvement in WPT Systems with Passive Auxiliary Circuits for Soft-switching
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper compares the efficiency and radiated EMI of conventional WPT systems and a system incorporating passive auxiliary circuits for soft switching. The experimental results indicate that the proposed system improved the efficiency by 0.68 percentage points and achieved an average reduction of 5.36 dBμA in the strength of radiated EMI.

articleTitle: Analytical loss model for single- and two-speed electric vehicle gearboxes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper investigates load-dependent and load-independent power losses of clutchless dual-stage single- and two-speed gearboxes for a subcompact electric vehicle (EV). The load-dependent loss includes gear meshing and bearing friction losses, whereas the load-independent loss encompasses gear churning, bearing drag and oil lip seal sources of loss. The methodology proposed estimates these losses based on the geometric parameters and dynamic characteristics of the gears and bearings and lubricant properties. A single-speed production EV gearbox was disassembled to determine the bearing, gear, and lubrication characteristics. The proposed analytical model is applied to estimate power losses for this gearbox as a function of electric machine speed and torque. Additionally, a second gear is added, making the gearbox two-speed, resulting in increased loss but providing the opportunity for increased electric machine and inverter efficiency. The single-speed gearbox has a 7.05:1 final ratio, while the two-speed variant has 7.05:1 and 4.2:1 for the first and second gears. At lower torques, where an EV would operate most, the single-speed gearbox has an efficiency between 94 and 97%, and the two-speed gearbox has between 0.1% and 0.7% lower efficiency when operating in first gear (the same 7.05:1 ratio as for the single-speed gearbox). When at low torque in second gear, the gearbox is about 1 percent more efficient for highway driving conditions, an important contribution towards extending vehicle range. The analysis also shows gear oil immersion depth significantly affects churning loss, and oil temperature has a small effect on overall gearbox loss.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Analysis of Electric Vehicle System Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: There are several figures used to promote the energy efficiency of battery electric vehicles (BEVs). A critical analysis of the energy consumption of BEV systems is presented here. A typical approach to estimate the efficiency of BEVs is to use fixed values for each component. Often the best possible value is taken in use. In practice, the efficiencies vary as a function of the operation point of the device and ambient conditions where the EV is used. It is also important to remember that propulsion is just part of the energy consumption in a modern EV and other consumers like air conditioning may use a high share of energy. The range of efficiency of each stage of an EV system is presented and the influential factors are discussed.

articleTitle: Safety-Critical Generalized Predictive Control for PMSM Drives Based on Control Barrier Function
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper presents a novel safety-critical generalized predictive control (SCGPC) strategy for speed regulation of permanent synchronous motor (PMSM) drives with a non-cascade structure. The proposed approach incorporates a robust control barrier function (RCBF) to explicitly consider the current constraint, addressing the constraint deviation problem caused by disturbances through a disturbance estimation and compensation technique. By solving an optimization problem, the RCBF-based current constraint mechanism and the generalized predictive control (GPC)-based speed controller are unified, combining the advantages of GPC and model predictive control (MPC). The integrated approach achieves efficient calculation without imposing a high computational burden, while simultaneously ensuring fast-tracking of the desired speed and strict adherence to current constraint. Both simulation and experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach when compared to traditional MPC and GPC methods.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian-Differential Flatness Control Laws for Battery/Ultracapacitor for Hybrid Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: This paper introduces the Hamiltonian-differential flatness control laws specifically designed for battery and ultracapacitor (UC) hybrid vehicle systems. The main goal of these control laws is to effectively manage power flow and optimize energy utilization in hybrid systems combining batteries and UC. The proposed control laws use Hamiltonian control and differential flatness techniques to dynamically regulate the energy distribution between the battery and UC, particularly in the context of constant power load (CPL) challenges within DC Microgrid applications, including vehicle systems. To confirm the efficiency of the proposed control strategy, the experimental test bench has been set up with a Li-ion battery module (LFeLi-48100TB, 48 Vdc, 100 Ah) and a UC module with a capacitance of (188.88 F, 51.3 V.) Finally, the experimental results confirm the exceptional performance of the studied control law throughout the load-drive cycles.

articleTitle: Analysis of cell-level abnormality diagnosis based on battery pack voltage information
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo, Asia-Pacific (ITEC Asia-Pacific)
abstract: Efficient and secure battery management is essential to optimize the performance and life of battery-powered systems.
